result.bio: Jean-Luc Mélenchon is a French politician born in 1951. He was a Socialist Party senator and minister, left the PS in 2008 and co-founded the Parti de Gauche, then founded La France insoumise (LFI) in 2016. He sat as MEP from 2009 to 2017 and as deputy for Bouches-du-Rhône from 2017 to 2022, and has run for president in 2012, 2017 (fourth) and 2022 (third). He announced on 3 May 2026 (per English Wikipedia) a fourth candidacy for 2027, built on an update of L'Avenir en commun and a Sixth Republic.

offices.office: Conseiller général de l'Essonne et président délégué du conseil général (not president)
Ministre délégué à l'Enseignement professionnel (gouvernement Jospin)
Député des Bouches-du-Rhône; président du groupe LFI
Fondateur et leader de LFI (Parti de Gauche co-founder 2008)

legal.case: Rebellion and provocation after the October 2018 searches of LFI premises and his home: sentenced in December 2019 to 3 months suspended plus 8,000 EUR fine. Appeal and cassation outcome not verified in this session (French Wikipedia summary mentions appeal and cassation proceedings); treat finality as unconfirmed.

European Parliament assistants affair (embezzlement of EP funds, 2009-2017, OLAF 2017, judicial investigation from 2018): judges closed the instruction on 26-27 May 2026 without any mise en examen of Mélenchon; two former assistants keep témoin assisté status; no evidence of his direct involvement or an organised scheme was established.

reversals.before: Voted for Maastricht in 1992 as a left compromise; PS insider favourable to European integration.
reversals.after: Campaigned against the 2005 constitutional treaty, later 'Plan A / Plan B': renegotiate the treaties or disobey them, 'ni Frexit, ni Europe libérale'; regrets his Maastricht stance.

reversals.before: 2014: described the annexation of Crimea as 'absolutely predictable'.
reversals.after: 2022: condemned the invasion; later accepted arms for Ukraine's defence while opposing deeper French involvement and favouring non-alignment/distance from NATO.

reversals.before: Earlier in his career broadly supportive of nuclear (as PS minister/senator).
reversals.after: Programme calls for exit from nuclear by 2050 with 100% renewables; internal LFI debate persists. Nuance: dating of the earlier position is from a single secondary summary.

reversals.before: Rhetoric closer to 'welcoming' migration policy and regularisation, a position LFI still formally holds.
reversals.after: Has toned down free movement of workers, citing social dumping (per a secondary aggregator; weak sourcing, a nuance more than a clear reversal).

delivery.what: Minister for vocational education 2000-2002: reformed vocational certificates and introduced validation of acquired experience (VAE).
delivery.assessment: Neutral encyclopedic source credits a pragmatic reformist record; limited and dated, with no sources of other leanings consulted in this session.

delivery.what: Led the LFI parliamentary group 2017-2021 and built NUPES in 2022 (the left union that won about 150 seats), then inspired the 2024 NFP alliance without holding a mandate himself.
delivery.assessment: Strong opposition and coalition-building result, but no executive power obtained; roll-call votes were not checked in this session.

delivery.what: Programme for 2027: SMIC at 1,600 EUR net, retirement at 60, price freezes, stronger wealth tax, Sixth Republic via constituent assembly, nuclear exit by 2050.
delivery.assessment: Promises only, derived from aggregator summaries of L'Avenir en commun; costing disputed between left think-tanks and liberal ones, which was not verified here.

traits.evidence: Wikipedia-type neutral sources call him a 'firebrand leader'; the 2019 conviction arose from a confrontation with police; right-leaning outlets (CNews, JDD) and the neutral encyclopedic source portray a combative style. Only partially cross-checked, since the search budget ran out.

traits.trait: Gifted orator / tribune with strong party control
traits.evidence: Described as a left-populist leader who dominates LFI; neutral and left-leaning self-presentations agree on his oratory. Corroboration limited.

media_portrayal.left_media: Left outlets present him as the principal voice of social rupture and ecological planning, and see judicial cases (searches, EP assistants) as political harassment; LFI itself said the May 2026 closure confirms no infraction occurred. Not directly sampled in this session.
media_portrayal.right_media: CNews and JDD cover him mainly through legal troubles, the 2018 raid and conviction, and the assistants affair, stressing the estimated 500,000 EUR loss, even while reporting the closure without indictment.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Neutral and institutional sources (Wikipedia, Telos, L'Essentiel) describe a democratic-socialist/left-populist who was not charged in the assistants case, unlike Le Pen (convicted) and Bayrou (acquitted).

result.sources_note: Search budget (200 WebSearch calls) was exhausted mid-task, so the research is thinner than required: no roll-call votes (datan/nosdeputes), no primary programme text, no opened Le Monde, Libération or Mediapart pages, and the 2019 conviction's appeal/cassation outcome is unverified. Relied on JDD and CNews (right) for the assistants case, Telos and L'Essentiel (neutral/centre), English and French Wikipedia, and election aggregators (elyseescope, testpolitique, monvote2027), which are secondary and of uncertain lean. Treat reversals, traits and delivery as provisional and re-check before use.

result.bio: Marine Le Pen (born 1968) is a French lawyer-turned-politician who led the Front national, renamed Rassemblement national (RN) in 2018, from 2011 to 2021. She reached the presidential runoff in 2017 and 2022 and has chaired the RN group in the Assemblée nationale since 2022. She was convicted in March 2025 and again on appeal in July 2026 in the European Parliament assistants case. On 7 July 2026 she announced her fourth presidential candidacy; Jordan Bardella, who had been the backup candidate, withdrew in her favour.

offices.office: President of the Front national / Rassemblement national
Co-president, Europe of Nations and Freedoms group (European Parliament)
President of the RN group, Assemblée nationale

legal.case: European Parliament parliamentary assistants case (embezzlement of EU public funds). First instance, 31 March 2025: 4 years (2 firm), EUR 100,000 fine, 5 years' ineligibility with immediate execution. Appeal, 7 July 2026: 1 year firm under electronic monitoring plus a suspended portion (reported as 3 years in total, 2 suspended), EUR 100,000 fine, 45 months' ineligibility of which 30 suspended. The court found no personal enrichment, with funds benefiting the party. The 15 firm months of ineligibility were already served, so she is eligible in 2027. Other defendants include Louis Aliot (1 year suspended), Bruno Gollnisch (3 years suspended) and Julien Odoul (8 months suspended). The RN was fined EUR 2 million (EUR 1 million suspended). A cassation appeal has been filed. Briefs are due by 15 Oct 2026. The Court of Cassation says it 'could' rule by early April 2027, which is provisional, and the first round is on 18 April 2027. The conviction is therefore not final.

reversals.before: 2017 campaign: proposed leaving the euro and returning to a national currency, via a referendum.
reversals.after: 2022: said she did not want to take France out of the eurozone and dropped euro exit from her programme.

reversals.before: 2007: defended retirement at 65. 2012 and 2017: return to 60.
reversals.after: 2022: 60 to 62 depending on career start. 27 Aug 2026: keeps a return to 62 with 42 years of contributions, and 60 with 40 years for early starters. This is a refinement rather than a clear reversal, and is partly counted here as a historical shift.

reversals.before: 2011: said she admired Putin 'to a certain extent'. 2014-2017: aligned with Russian discourse on Crimea and favoured lifting sanctions.
reversals.after: After February 2022: condemns the invasion 'without ambiguity' but opposes further financial aid to Ukraine on budget grounds, and still defends the Crimea referendum. The shift is partial.

delivery.what: No national or local executive office held. Her output is legislative and party-building: leading the RN group (since 2022), a bloc of roughly 120+ deputies after the 2024 elections, as the largest single party in the Assemblée. She has also presided over the party's 'dédiabolisation', including expelling her father and renaming the FN as RN in 2018.
delivery.assessment: Left and centre-left sources describe dédiabolisation as cosmetic. Right-wing and neutral outlets credit it with mainstreaming the party. Detailed roll-call vote analysis (datan.fr, nosdeputes.fr) was not retrieved in this session.

delivery.what: 2027 programme (shared with Bardella): national preference in social benefits and social housing, VAT on energy cut from 20% to 5.5%, income tax exemption for under-30s, minimum sentences for recidivists, expulsion of foreign offenders, return to retirement at 62.
delivery.assessment: Financing relies largely on hoped-for savings from sharply reduced immigration. A pensions measure was costed at about EUR 9 billion. These costings come from secondary aggregator sites and should be treated cautiously.

traits.trait: Strategic party-manager who prioritises image and 'dédiabolisation' (expelled her father, renamed the party)
traits.evidence: Widely reported across encyclopaedic, neutral and French outlets, and framed as a deliberate normalisation strategy.

traits.trait: Combative and confrontational toward the political and judicial establishment
traits.evidence: Frames her conviction as political and the ineligibility as a 'political decision' (reported in coverage of the verdict); also reflected in her parliamentary style.

traits.trait: Dynastic or personally controlling leadership of the RN
traits.evidence: France 24 describes her 2026 candidacy as a 'dynastic' choice that eclipses Bardella.

media_portrayal.left_media: Portrayed as the head of a far-right party whose 'normalisation' is cosmetic, and as a convicted embezzler. Her Russian ties and the national-preference programme are emphasised. This is inferred from general patterns, as left-leaning outlets (Libération, Mediapart, L'Humanité) were not fetched directly in this session.
media_portrayal.right_media: Portrayed as a legitimate populist or sovereigntist leader targeted by a judicial system seen as politicised, with her programme on immigration, security and purchasing power framed favourably. This is inferred, as CNews and Europe 1 were seen only as search snippets or related items.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: France 24, franceinfo, LCP and Public Sénat report the verdict and eligibility in procedural detail, stress the legal uncertainty before the cassation ruling, and treat the Le Pen/Bardella arrangement as a strategic question for the RN.

result.sources_note: Research was cut short because the WebSearch budget was exhausted after about 7 queries in this session. Outlets actually seen or opened: Public Sénat, LCP, franceinfo, France 24, Touteleurope, Le Grand Continent, Europe 1, Euronews, Journal du Net, CNews and JDD (search snippets only), Wikipedia. Gaps: no primary roll-call analysis (datan.fr, howtheyvote.eu), the 2022 programme and RN site were not opened, and the 2012 campaign-financing and other secondary cases were not verified, so the legal list is limited to the assistants case. Wikipedia's fr summary gave a different sentence breakdown ('1 year firm + 3 years suspended') from other sources ('3 years, 2 suspended'); the Public Sénat headline is retained for the firm year. Several programme figures come from aggregator sites. Lean labels for media_portrayal and traits are partly inferred from general patterns.

result.bio: Bruno Retailleau (born 20 November 1960 in Cholet) is a conservative politician from the Vendée, senator since 2004 and president of Les Républicains since May 2025. He chaired the Vendée departmental council and the Pays de la Loire region, led the LR Senate group, and served as Interior Minister in the Barnier and Bayrou governments (Sept 2024 - Oct 2025). He declared his 2027 presidential candidacy in February 2026 and won the LR nomination on 19 April 2026. He is known for a restrictive line on immigration and security and for socially conservative positions.

result.bio: Éric Zemmour, born 31 August 1958 in Montreuil, is a French journalist, essayist and politician. He worked at Le Figaro, RTL, Paris Première and CNews before founding Reconquête in December 2021. He finished fourth in the 2022 presidential election with 7.07% and confirmed his 2027 candidacy on BFM TV on 17 September 2026. Reconquête is classed as far-right and national-conservative, and campaigns on "zero immigration", assimilation and Euroscepticism.

offices.office: Candidate in Var 4th constituency (eliminated first round, 23.19%)

delivery.assessment: Founded a durable party and brought immigration and identity to the centre of debate, but won no seats in 2022. result.bio: Olivier Faure (born 18 August 1968 in La Tronche, Isère) is a French Socialist politician, a PS member since 1984 and deputy for Seine-et-Marne's 11th constituency since 2012. He has led the Parti socialiste as First Secretary since April 2018 and was re-elected in 2021, 2023 and June 2025. He backed the NUPES alliance in 2022 and the Nouveau Front populaire in 2024, and negotiated a common-candidate process with other left parties. He announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential nomination on 30 August 2026 and published the book "La loi du plus juste" in September 2026.

result.bio: Marine Tondelier (born 23 August 1986, Bois-Bernard, Pas-de-Calais) is National Secretary of Les Écologistes since December 2022, re-elected in April 2025. She trained at Sciences Po Lille, led the air-quality federation Atmo France (2017-2022), and has sat as an opposition councillor in Hénin-Beaumont since 2014 and as a Hauts-de-France regional councillor since 2021. She announced her 2027 presidential candidacy on 22 October 2025 and was designated by her party on 8 December 2025.

legal.case: Defamation suit by Hénin-Beaumont mayor Steeve Briois and Bruno Bilde (RN) over her 2017 book Nouvelles du Front; she was the defendant

reversals.before: Called for France to leave or shut down X, citing election disinformation and gender-based violence
reversals.after: Reversed within about a week and stayed on X, saying she would defend ecology on 'hostile terrain'

delivery.what: Led the party as National Secretary and was re-elected with 72.64% in April 2025 after internal criticism over congress rules. She has never held national or local executive office, so there is no legislative or ministerial record.
delivery.assessment: Party-management record only. Critics inside the party include Sandrine Rousseau (Feb 2025, 'apparatchik reflexes') and a tribune of more than 500 members (Jan-Feb 2026) against her municipal alliance strategy. result.bio: François Ruffin, born 18 October 1975 in Calais, is a journalist, documentary maker, essayist and politician. He founded the local newspaper Fakir in 1999 and directed the documentary Merci patron! (2016, César for best documentary 2017). He has been deputy for Somme's 1st constituency since 2017 and sat with the LFI group until 2024, though he never formally joined the party. He broke with Jean-Luc Mélenchon in July 2024, became president of Debout ! on 28 June 2025 and, per Wikipedia, announced a bid for the left primary and then a presidential run after that primary was cancelled.

offices.office: Deputy for Somme, 1st constituency (elected 2017, re-elected 2022 and 2024)
Secretary of the Economic Affairs Commission, Assemblée nationale

legal.case: Civil defamation ruling by the Amiens tribunal over statements in his book Quartier Nord about neighbourhood residents (Wikipedia describes him as found liable)
Victim, not accused: Mediapart reported LVMH hired Kyrnos (Bernard Squarcini) to surveil Ruffin and Fakir in 2015-2016. Arnault denied involvement. Judicial outcome unclear in the source.
HATVP reported a EUR 431,973 undervaluation of his audiovisual production company in his asset declaration. No criminal proceedings are reported in the source.

delivery.what: Merci patron! documentary (2016) on the LVMH/Arnault case, which won a César. Parliamentary work includes a high volume of amendments (4,098 rejected in the first year) and the SMIC-salary pledge, with most of his parliamentary pay passed to associations and the PCF.
delivery.assessment: Wikipedia reports high amendment volume but low early attendance (22% in his first year). Few of his own texts have been passed. I could not do a roll-call vote review or find any balanced outlet assessment because the web search budget ran out.

delivery.what: Initiated the Nouveau Front populaire coalition in June 2024 and then left LFI on 4 July 2024.
delivery.assessment: Described as a strategic split with Mélenchon. No outlet of differing lean was consulted.

traits.trait: Independent, populist-left, protectionist positioning bridging working-class and intellectual left
traits.evidence: Wikipedia summary of his stances and media portrayal. Only one source, so this does not meet the two-source threshold.

media_portrayal.right_media: Not verified. Search was unavailable.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Per Wikipedia: increasingly independent, bridging popular classes and the intellectual left. Criticised over low attendance, ethics episodes at Fakir (2017) and accusations of dog-whistles (2018) that he disputed.

result.bio: Fabien Roussel (born 16 April 1969 in Béthune) is a former L'Humanité and France Télévisions journalist who became national secretary of the PCF in November 2018. He was deputy for Nord's 20th constituency from 2017 to 2024 and the PCF's 2022 presidential candidate (2.28%, 8th place). He lost his seat to the RN in 2024 and became mayor of Saint-Amand-les-Eaux in January 2025. According to Wikipedia he announced his 2027 candidacy on 6 September 2026 under the slogan "Vivre", after an internal party consultation.

offices.office: National secretary (secrétaire national) of the PCF

legal.case: Mediapart (2022) alleged a fictitious parliamentary-assistant job with deputy Jean-Jacques Candelier (2009-2014). The Parquet National Financier opened a preliminary investigation. Roussel denies the allegation. Candelier said in L'Humanité that Roussel was indeed his assistant.

reversals.before: Favoured leaving NATO or its integrated command, in line with the traditional PCF line.
reversals.after: After the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022 he no longer proposes withdrawal from NATO. Unlike Mélenchon, Arthaud and Poutou, he does not call for leaving it.

delivery.what: Deputy 2017-2024 (opposition, PCF group). Pushed the SMIC at 1,500 euros net, retirement at 60 and a higher wealth tax. No major law passed under his name is documented in the sources I could access.
delivery.assessment: His platform is consistently left-economic, with distinctive stances on nuclear power, security and 'work-focused' left themes. I could not verify a legislative record from roll-call sites (datan.fr, nosdeputes.fr) because search was unavailable.

delivery.what: Mayor of Saint-Amand-les-Eaux since January 2025. His reported 2026 municipal result is a first-round win with 51.06%.
delivery.assessment: Recent executive record is short, and no assessment of his term was found in the sources I could access.

result.bio: David Lisnard, born 2 February 1969 in Limoges, is a Sciences Po Bordeaux graduate who has been mayor of Cannes since April 2014 (re-elected 2020 and 2026). He was president of the Association des maires de France from November 2021 and was re-elected in November 2023. He belonged to the RPR, UMP and Les Républicains, and was LR vice-president from June 2025. He left LR on 31 March 2026. He announced on RTL on 21 January 2026 that he would run for president in 2027, under the banner of his movement Nouvelle Énergie. The movement was founded in 2014 and launched nationally in June 2021. A June 2026 Ifop poll gave him about 2% in the first round.

legal.case: Cannes burkini ban order (Aug 2016). The Conseil d'Etat ruled similar bans illegal on 26 Aug 2016, and in May 2018 the city was ordered to reimburse a fine. This is an administrative ruling against the municipality, not a criminal case against him personally.

reversals.topic: Party loyalty and the LR primary
reversals.before: A member of the RPR, UMP and then LR for about 30 years. He was LR vice-president from June 2025 and took part in LR's internal debates.
reversals.after: Left LR on 31 March 2026 after opposing its primary process, and declared an independent candidacy.

delivery.what: Cannes municipal management: debt reduced by about 55.5 million euros (2014-2019) and one of France's densest video-surveillance networks, with a reorganised municipal police.
delivery.assessment: These are the figures his own camp and the sources used here present as achievements. The sources used here contain no critical assessment of them, so the balance is limited.

delivery.assessment: Both episodes were criticised as legally invalid or ineffective. The burkini ruling is documented, with the Conseil d'Etat decision and the 2018 reimbursement.

result.bio: Jean-Luc Mélenchon is a French politician born in 1951. He was a Socialist Party senator for Essonne and minister delegate for vocational education (2000-2002), left the PS in 2008 to co-found the Parti de Gauche, and founded La France insoumise (LFI) in 2016. He sat as an MEP from 2009 to 2017 and as deputy for Bouches-du-Rhône from 2017 to 2022, and ran for president in 2012 (fourth), 2017 (fourth) and 2022 (third). He announced a fourth candidacy, for 2027, on TF1 on 3 May 2026, on a platform built on an update of L'Avenir en commun and a Sixth Republic.

offices.office: Conseiller général de l'Essonne (canton de Massy-Ouest)
Conseiller général de l'Essonne et président délégué du conseil général (not president, so not counted in executive years)
Ministre délégué à l'Enseignement professionnel (gouvernement Jospin)
Président du groupe LFI à l'Assemblée nationale
Co-founder of the Parti de Gauche (2008-2009), then founder and leader of La France insoumise

legal.case: Rebellion and provocation following the altercation with police during the October 2018 searches of LFI headquarters: sentenced on 9 December 2019 by the Bobigny criminal court to three months' suspended prison and an 8,000 EUR fine. No appeal reversal is reported by English or French Wikipedia; final status could not be checked against a court or AFP source in this session.

European Parliament assistants affair (suspected misuse of EP funds for assistants, complaint 2017, judicial investigation opened November 2018). The investigating judges closed the instruction on 26-27 May 2026 without placing Mélenchon under formal investigation (mise en examen); he was never charged. Two former assistants keep témoin assisté status. Since no one can be sent to trial without a mise en examen, he will not face trial in this case (AFP via L'Essentiel). Telos notes that no evidence established his direct involvement or an organised scheme. The formal final order was not reported in the sources consulted.

reversals.before: 1992: called for a yes vote on the Maastricht treaty, describing it as a 'leftist compromise' (paraphrase, French Wikipedia).
reversals.after: He soon regretted that vote and later said the treaty's opponents had been right. He campaigned against the 2005 constitutional treaty. His 2027 line is 'Plan A / Plan B': renegotiate the treaties and disobey them if that fails, without formally advocating Frexit.

delivery.what: Minister delegate for vocational education, 2000-2002: reformed vocational certificates (CAP), worked on validation of acquired experience (VAE), and created the 'lycée des métiers' label.
delivery.assessment: Described by a neutral encyclopedic source. VAE was enacted in the January 2002 social modernisation law, which was a government-wide text, so how much of it was his own contribution was not checked. No sources of other leanings were consulted.

delivery.what: Chaired the LFI parliamentary group from 2017 to 2021 and led the formation of NUPES in 2022, a left alliance that won about 150 seats. He did not stand for re-election as deputy in 2022.
delivery.assessment: This is an opposition and coalition-building record with no executive power. Roll-call votes were not checked in this session.

delivery.what: 2027 programme: minimum wage (SMIC) at 1,600 EUR net, retirement at 60 after 40 years of contributions, price freezes on essentials and energy, a stronger wealth tax, a Sixth Republic via an elected constituent assembly, and a nuclear exit with 100% renewables by 2050.
delivery.assessment: These are promises only, taken from a secondary aggregator summary of L'Avenir en commun. The primary programme text and independent costings were not checked.

media_portrayal.left_media: Left-leaning outlets and LFI typically present him as the main voice of social rupture and ecological planning, and frame the judicial cases as political harassment. LFI said the May 2026 closure 'confirms what we have maintained from the start'. Left outlets were not sampled directly in this session.
media_portrayal.right_media: Right-leaning outlets such as JDD and CNews cover him largely through his legal cases (the 2018 searches and the 2019 conviction, and the EP assistants affair), while also reporting that the instruction closed without a mise en examen.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Neutral sources (Wikipedia, Telos, AFP via L'Essentiel) describe a left-populist leader, often called polarising, who was not charged in the EP assistants case. They contrast this with Le Pen, convicted on appeal, and Bayrou, acquitted.

result.sources_note: Verification pass made under a hard limit: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so checks used direct fetches only. Confirmed by fetch: English and French Wikipedia (offices and dates, the 3 May 2026 TF1 candidacy announcement, the Maastricht stance), JDD (right), AFP via L'Essentiel (neutral), Telos (centrist think-tank), and the aggregators monvote2027, elyseescope (Europe page), testpolitique and candidats-presidentielle-2027 (uncertain lean, secondary). The CNews page returned HTTP 403 and was removed. No roll-call votes, primary programme text, or Le Monde, franceinfo, Libération or Mediapart pages were consulted. Whether the 2019 conviction is final rests on the absence of any reported appeal reversal, without a court or AFP confirmation. Re-check before publication.

result.bio: Édouard Philippe (born 1970) is a French centre-right politician and founder of Horizons (2021). He was Prime Minister under Emmanuel Macron from May 2017 to July 2020 and has been mayor of Le Havre since July 2020, a post he also held from 2010 to 2017; he was re-elected mayor in March 2026. He announced his 2027 presidential candidacy in September 2024 (in Le Point) and launched his campaign in Paris on 5 July 2026 with the slogan "Croire en nous". He stepped down as Horizons president on 9 September 2026 to build a broader coalition, and Christophe Béchu took over on 1 October 2026.

offices.office: Mayor of Le Havre (second spell, re-elected 2026-03-28)
President of Le Havre Seine Métropole

legal.case: Cour de justice de la République judicial investigation into the government's management of the Covid-19 pandemic, opened 7 July 2020 and covering Édouard Philippe, Agnès Buzyn and Olivier Véran; his home was searched on 15 October 2020. His procedural status as of October 2026 (for example témoin assisté or mis en examen) and whether the case has been closed could not be verified. No charge or conviction is documented in the sources consulted. He is presumed innocent.

In 2014 the HATVP (the public-ethics authority) published a critical assessment of his asset declaration. He had not given property values and had not disclosed his fees as a lawyer or his pay from Areva. He later updated the declaration. This was an administrative assessment, not a judicial case.

reversals.topic: PMA (assisted reproduction) for single women and female couples
reversals.before: In a 2013 opinion piece he opposed opening PMA to single women and female couples.
reversals.after: As Prime Minister his government carried the bioethics bill that extended PMA, and he said he had "évolué sur cette question" (paraphrased in the source as "evolved on this question").

reversals.before: From 2014 to early 2017 he criticised Macron publicly. In 2014 he called him a former Rothschild banker, and in early 2017 he spoke of the cynicism of a seasoned operator (paraphrase).
reversals.after: He became Macron's Prime Minister in May 2017. From autumn 2025 he distanced himself again: he called the 2024 dissolution a "décision funeste et absurde" and repeatedly called on the president to resign.

delivery.what: 2019-2020 universal points-based pension reform: he used Article 49.3 to adopt the bill without a vote, which the opposition denounced as forcing it through
delivery.assessment: The source confirms the 49.3 use, the opposition's charge that it forced the bill through, and his long-standing support for raising the legal retirement age from 62 to 65, 66 or 67 and merging all pension schemes, which he presented as a way to reduce the public debt. A balanced assessment from sources of different leanings was not obtained.

delivery.assessment: This is a summary only. The page confirms these reform areas but the detail was not retrievable, and cross-leaning assessments were not obtained.

delivery.what: Nationwide 80 km/h speed limit on secondary roads (July 2018)
delivery.assessment: According to the source he was personally involved in the measure, against Macron's preferences, and it is reported to have fed the Gilets jaunes movement. Cross-leaning assessments were not obtained.

All content comes from three French Wikipedia pages, which were re-fetched and checked during verification: Édouard Philippe, Horizons (parti politique) and Gouvernement Édouard Philippe (2). result.bio: Marine Le Pen (born 1968) is a French lawyer-turned-politician who led the Front national, renamed Rassemblement national (RN) in 2018, from 2011 to 2021. She reached the presidential runoff in 2017 and 2022, has been deputy for Pas-de-Calais since 2017, and has chaired the RN group in the Assemblée nationale since 2022. She was convicted of embezzlement of public funds in the European Parliament assistants case at first instance in March 2025 and on appeal on 7 July 2026; she has appealed to the Court of Cassation, so the conviction is not final. On 7 July 2026 she announced her fourth presidential candidacy; RN president Jordan Bardella, who had been presented as the alternative candidate, launched the campaign alongside her on 8 July.

offices.office: President of the Front national / Rassemblement national
Co-president, Europe of Nations and Freedoms group (European Parliament)
Departmental councillor, Pas-de-Calais (canton Hénin-Beaumont-2); removed ex officio after the 2025 ineligibility, confirmed by the Conseil d'État on 10 Nov 2025
President of the RN group, Assemblée nationale

legal.case: European Parliament parliamentary assistants case (embezzlement of public funds). First instance, Paris criminal court, 31 March 2025: 4 years' prison (2 firm under electronic monitoring), EUR 100,000 fine, 5 years' ineligibility with provisional execution. Appeal, Paris Court of Appeal, 7 July 2026: guilt confirmed, sentence reduced to 3 years' prison (1 year firm as home detention under electronic monitoring, 2 years suspended), EUR 100,000 fine, 45 months' ineligibility of which 30 suspended. The 15 firm months of ineligibility had expired on 30 June 2026, so she is eligible in 2027. The court found that only the party benefited from the misappropriated funds. Co-defendants on appeal include Louis Aliot (1 year suspended, EUR 5,000 fine, 2 years' suspended ineligibility), Bruno Gollnisch (3 years suspended, EUR 25,000 fine, 1 year ineligibility) and Julien Odoul (8 months suspended, 1 year suspended ineligibility); the RN was fined EUR 2 million (EUR 1 million suspended) plus EUR 1 million confiscation. She has lodged an appeal in cassation, which suspends execution of the prison term. On 8 July 2026 the Court of Cassation said it 'could' rule 'at the latest early April 2027', adding that the timetable may change for procedural reasons; the first round is on 18 April 2027. The conviction is not final.

Judicial investigation (information judiciaire) opened July 2024, after referrals by the campaign-finance commission (CNCCFP), into suspected illegal financing of her 2022 presidential campaign, the 2022 legislative and 2024 European campaigns (loans from a legal entity to a candidate, embezzlement, fraud, forgery). The RN headquarters was searched on 9 July 2025. No indictment (mise en examen) of Marine Le Pen personally was found in the sources checked.

Public insult on grounds of origin or religion (2019 European campaign post linking a 'young European of the year' laureate to radical Islam). Tried in Paris on 10 Nov 2025; acquitted (relaxée) in January 2026. Whether the prosecution appealed was not verified.

Defamation of the NGO La Cimade (accused it in a January 2022 TV interview of complicity with migrant smugglers from the Comoros to Mayotte). Convicted on 13 Oct 2023: EUR 500 suspended fine, EUR 1 damages, EUR 2,000 costs. Wikipedia reports the sentence was upheld on appeal and in cassation; those later rulings were not independently verified.
Incitement to racial hatred over a December 2010 speech comparing street prayers to an 'occupation'. Acquitted by the Lyon criminal court.

reversals.before: 2017 campaign: proposed returning to a national currency and leaving the euro (she softened this in late April 2017, toward a 'common euro' and a slower timetable).
reversals.after: 2022: dropped euro exit from her programme and no longer proposed leaving the eurozone.

reversals.before: Earlier presidential programmes: a general return to retirement at 60.
reversals.after: 2026 position for 2027: legal age of 62 for most workers; 60 only for those who started work before 20 and have 40 years of contributions. CNews describes this as a distinction by career start 'rather than a general return to 60'.

reversals.before: 2017: after meeting Putin at the Kremlin, called EU sanctions on Russia 'profoundly unjust and counterproductive' and considered lifting them; defended the 2014 Crimea vote.
reversals.after: After February 2022: condemns the invasion of Ukraine 'without ambiguity', while opposing further financial aid to Ukraine on budget grounds and still defending the Crimea referendum (2023 testimony). The shift is partial.

delivery.what: No national or local executive office held. Her record is legislative and party-building: she has led the RN group in the Assemblée nationale since 2022 (about 120 deputies after the 2024 elections, the largest single-party group). As party leader she pursued the 'dédiabolisation' (normalisation) strategy, which included excluding her father from the party in 2015 and renaming the FN as RN in 2018.
delivery.assessment: How effective and how deep dédiabolisation was is disputed. Le Figaro (centre-right) published the view that talk of a 'new FN' is 'political fiction'; L'Humanité (left) relayed SOS Racisme calling it a 'media-driven farce'. Encyclopaedic sources describe it as a deliberate strategy that broadened the party's electorate. No roll-call vote analysis (datan.fr, nosdeputes.fr) was retrieved.

delivery.what: Pensions proposal for 2027 (confirmed August-October 2026): legal retirement age of 62, and 60 for those who started work before 20 with 40 years of contributions. Bardella's position differed (dropping an age-based rule and adding a funded pillar), and adviser François Durvye resigned over the disagreement.
delivery.assessment: Le Pen puts the cost at about EUR 9 billion a year. Institut Montaigne (centre-right/liberal) estimates far more: EUR 26.5 billion a year in its basic scenario, up to EUR 38 billion. Other programme measures (national preference, energy VAT cut to 5.5%, income tax exemption for under-30s) come from the 2022 programme, and the updated 2027 versions were not verified in this session.

traits.trait: Strategic party manager focused on image and normalisation ('dédiabolisation')
traits.evidence: Outlets of different leanings describe dédiabolisation as her deliberate strategy, whether they treat it as real or cosmetic: Le Figaro (centre-right), L'Humanité (left, relaying SOS Racisme), and encyclopaedic summaries. Concrete steps: excluding her father (2015) and renaming the party (2018).

media_portrayal.left_media: Left-leaning outlets (e.g. L'Humanité, Mediapart, Libération) tend to present her as leading a far-right party whose normalisation is mostly cosmetic, and focus on the embezzlement conviction, the party's links with former GUD figures and Russia, and the national-preference programme. This is based on headlines cited in reference works; recent left-leaning articles were not opened directly.
media_portrayal.right_media: Right-leaning outlets (e.g. CNews, JDD, Europe 1) tend to give prominence to her programme on immigration, security, pensions and purchasing power, and to give space to the argument that the judiciary is politicised. Only a CNews programme article was opened directly, so this is partly inferred.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Public Sénat, LCP, franceinfo, France 24 and Touteleurope report the verdict and her eligibility in procedural detail, stress the uncertainty before the cassation ruling, and treat the Le Pen/Bardella arrangement as a strategic question for the RN.

result.sources_note: Sources used: Public Sénat, LCP, franceinfo, France 24, Touteleurope (neutral or institutional); Le Grand Continent (Russia); Journal du Net and reference-entreprise.com (aggregators on pensions); CNews (right); Le Figaro (centre-right) and L'Humanité (left), on dédiabolisation; Euronews and Infobae (euro); Euronews and France 24 (earlier cases); French and English Wikipedia for offices and for some secondary cases. Caveats: the original research ran out of WebSearch budget, and verification relied on fetching known URLs. The appeal sentence was cross-checked in Public Sénat, Touteleurope and Wikipedia ('3 years, 1 firm, 2 suspended'). The secondary cases (2024 financing investigation, the 2026 acquittal for insult, the Cimade appeal and cassation) rest mainly on Wikipedia and should be confirmed against court or AFP reports. No roll-call vote data was used. Lean labels for media portrayal are partly inferred.

positions.summary: L'Avenir en commun proposes restoring and strengthening the ISF with a climate component; 2026 summaries of the 2027 programme keep a reinforced ISF.

sources.quote: "Rétablir et renforcer l'impôt de solidarité sur la fortune (ISF), incluant un volet climatique visant à taxer les gros pollueurs"
"rétablir l'impôt de solidarité sur la fortune, supprimé en 2018, dans une version élargie intégrant un volet climatique"
"ISF renforcé"

positions.nuance: Primary text is the 2022 programme; the 2025 edition chapters could not be fetched (403/404), but 2026 secondary summaries confirm it is kept.

positions.summary: LFI is among the left parties defending the Zucman tax; its own programme (reinforced ISF) goes further.

sources.quote: "L'ensemble de la gauche, le Parti communiste français, La France insoumise, Les Écologistes, le Parti socialiste et Place publique défendent la mise en œuvre de la taxe Zucman"

positions.nuance: Party-level support; no Mélenchon quote or roll-call vote verified in this pass. The ISF he proposes is broader than a 2% floor on fortunes above EUR 100m.

positions.summary: No direct statement on production taxes or employer contributions found; the programme orientation is to raise contributions and condition aid to firms, the opposite of competitiveness tax cuts.

sources.quote: "Augmenter de 0,25 point par an durant le quinquennat le taux de cotisation vieillesse"
"Créer une mission spéciale dressant le bilan des faveurs fiscales"

positions.nuance: Inferred from adjacent measures; no explicit position on production taxes or employer-contribution cuts was verified.

positions.summary: The programme proposes 'protectionnisme écologique et solidaire pour produire en France', including tariffs on ecological criteria and a border kilometre tax to deter relocations and distant imports.

sources.quote: "Instaurer des droits de douane sur des critères écologiques" ... "Instaurer une taxe kilométrique aux frontières de la France pour dissuader les délocalisations"

positions.nuance: Tariffs are framed on ecological and social criteria rather than as classic sector protection; the price-rise trade-off is not addressed. 2022 programme text; no 2026 revision found.

positions.summary: The programme reverses privatisations, explicitly of airports and motorways, and 2026 summaries list nationalising EDF, ADP and mutual banks.

sources.quote: "Revenir sur les privatisations (aéroports, autoroutes, Française des Jeux, etc.)"
"EDF, ADP, banques mutualistes, parfois télécoms"

positions.summary: Raise inheritance tax on the largest estates and cap inheritance at about EUR 12m, while restructuring in favour of modest transmissions.

sources.quote: "Augmenter les droits de succession sur les plus hauts patrimoines ... et créer un héritage maximal de 12 millions d'euros"
"une refonte des droits de succession favorable aux transmissions modestes"
"Augmenter les droits de succession sur les plus hauts patrimoines et créer un héritage maximal de 12 M€"

positions.nuance: He opposes a general cut and wants large rises at the top, but also proposes relief for modest transmissions, so the opposition is partial.

positions.summary: Retirement at 60 on a full pension after 40 years of contributions is a flagship measure.

sources.quote: "Restaurer le droit à la retraite à 60 ans à taux plein pour 40 annuités de cotisations"
"Retraite à 60 ans après 40 années de cotisation"

positions.nuance: Goes further than 62.

positions.summary: Opposes any rise in the retirement age and wants 60.

sources.quote: "Restaurer le droit à la retraite à 60 ans à taux plein pour 40 annuités de cotisations"
"Retraite à 60 ans après 40 années de cotisation"

positions.summary: Defends the existing pay-as-you-go system of intergenerational solidarity and finances pensions through higher contributions.

sources.quote: "Rien ne justifie de renoncer au système actuel, de solidarité intergénérationnelle avec garantie du niveau des pensions."

positions.nuance: Capitalisation is not named explicitly; the programme defends the pay-as-you-go system and restricts the reserve fund's investments.

positions.summary: Rejects austerity and would stop unilaterally applying EU budgetary rules that are incompatible with the programme.

sources.quote: "Cesser d'appliquer unilatéralement les normes incompatibles avec nos engagements écologiques et sociaux telles que ... les règles budgétaires"
"La dette publique est instrumentalisée pour justifier l'austérité et les privatisations."

positions.nuance: 2022 programme text. The draft's claim about a Sept 2026 debt-cancellation plan could not be verified and was removed.

positions.summary: The programme calls for recruiting more civil servants (e.g. in justice) and revaluing their pay.

sources.quote: "Planifier des moyens pour la justice et recruter davantage de fonctionnaires : magistrats, greffiers, agents de la protection judiciaire de la jeunesse"

positions.nuance: No explicit headcount figure found; the programme consistently argues for more public-service staff.

positions.summary: Rejects debt-driven austerity and proposes that the ECB convert the public debt it holds into perpetual zero-rate debt and buy back debt held on markets, alongside large public investment.

sources.quote: "Exiger de l'Union européenne que la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) transforme la part de dette des États qu'elle possède en dettes perpétuelles à taux nul"

positions.nuance: 2022 programme text. The draft's La Grande Conversation source (19 Aug 2026) covers foreign policy only and does not mention debt, so it was removed.

positions.summary: No explicit statement on a constitutional golden rule found; the programme would stop applying EU budgetary rules, which points to opposition.

sources.quote: "Cesser d'appliquer unilatéralement les normes incompatibles ... telles que ... les règles budgétaires"

positions.nuance: Inferred; no direct quote on the règle d'or.

positions.summary: Immediate rise of the SMIC to EUR 1,600 net, well above inflation.

sources.quote: "SMIC à 1 600€ net dès le premier jour"
"Porter immédiatement le SMIC mensuel à 1 400 euros nets"

positions.nuance: The figure rose from EUR 1,400 (2022) to EUR 1,600 (2026 summaries).

positions.summary: Wants to restore a protective unemployment insurance, reverse Macron's cuts and pay benefits from the first day.

sources.quote: "Refuser la réforme Macron : indemniser les chômeurs en fonction de leurs derniers salaires"

positions.nuance: 2022 programme; consistent with later LFI opposition to benefit cuts.

positions.summary: LFI opposes conditioning the RSA on activity hours and proposes an unconditional income floor at the poverty line.

sources.quote: "Créer une garantie d'autonomie qui permettra que nul ne soit privé de sa dignité pour vivre"

positions.nuance: The programme does not address RSA activity hours directly; opposition to the 15-hour rule is party line and was not verified via a roll-call.

positions.summary: Restore the 35-hour week immediately, move to 32 hours in arduous or night jobs, and encourage generalising 32 hours through collective bargaining.

sources.quote: "passer aux 32 heures dans les métiers pénibles ou de nuit, et favoriser leur généralisation par la négociation collective"

positions.nuance: 2022 text; the legal duration stays at 35h, with 32h generalised through bargaining. A 2026 summary (TestPolitique) did not mention it.

positions.summary: Wants to make visas easier, regularise many undocumented people and make the 10-year card the reference permit; refuses numerical caps.

sources.quote: "Faciliter l'accès aux visas, régulariser les travailleurs, étudiants, parents d'enfants scolarisés"
Paraphrase: refuses any numerical limits on legal immigration; supports easier family reunification.

positions.summary: No evidence found on a referendum specifically about immigration policy.
positions.nuance: He supports a broad RIC (citizens' initiative referendum), which would in principle allow one; no statement for or against an immigration referendum was verified.

positions.summary: Opposes abolishing or restricting the AME and calls restrictions counterproductive for public health.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: opposes AME suppression; describes restrictions as counterproductive for public health.

positions.nuance: Aggregator summary; no roll-call vote or direct quote verified.

positions.summary: Regularise undocumented workers, students and parents of schooled children.

sources.quote: "régulariser les travailleurs, étudiants, parents d'enfants scolarisés"
Paraphrase: supports automatic regularisation for workers, students and family members.

positions.nuance: Broader than labour-shortage occupations.

positions.summary: The programme treats the universality of rights as non-negotiable, which is incompatible with national preference.

sources.quote: "L'universalité des droits n'est pas négociable en République"

positions.nuance: National preference is not named explicitly in the text verified.

positions.summary: Guarantee full droit du sol for all children born in France and make access to nationality easier.

sources.quote: "Garantir le droit du sol intégral à tous les enfants nés en France et faciliter l'accès à la nationalité française"

positions.nuance: 2022 programme text.

positions.summary: Give foreign residents the vote in local elections.

sources.quote: "Instituer le droit de vote des étrangers aux élections locales"
Paraphrase: supports granting regular foreign residents voting rights in municipal elections.

positions.nuance: Limited to legally resident foreigners, per MonVote2027.

positions.summary: Opposes mandatory minimum sentences and favours rehabilitation, prevention and alternatives to prison.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: opposes minimum mandatory sentences; defends rehabilitation and prevention over automatic sanctions.

positions.nuance: The MonVote2027 page states opposition but does not document a roll-call vote; the programme's justice section does not mention peines planchers.

positions.summary: Defends the principles of the 1945 juvenile-justice ordinance and rejects trying 16-year-olds as adults.

sources.quote: "Garantir le respect des principes de l'ordonnance de février 1945 sur l'enfance en conflit avec la loi"
Paraphrase: rejects trying minors as adults from age 16.

positions.summary: Abolish the IGPN and IGGN and replace them with an independent authority attached to the Défenseur des droits, with its own disciplinary powers.

sources.quote: "Supprimer l'Inspection générale de la Police nationale (IGPN) ... et les remplacer par une autorité indépendante"
Paraphrase: replace IGPN/IGGN with an independent authority under the Défenseur des droits.

positions.summary: Legalise recreational cannabis and regulate it through a state monopoly.

sources.quote: "Légaliser et encadrer par un monopole d'État la consommation, la production et la vente de cannabis à des fins récréatives"
"Légaliser et encadrer par un monopole d'État la vente, production et consommation de cannabis à des fins récréatives"

positions.nuance: 2021-2022 sources; no newer statement found.

positions.summary: The programme would ban facial-recognition technology in public spaces, including experiments.

sources.quote: "Interdire dans la loi tout usage des technologies de reconnaissance faciale dans les espaces et établissements publics"

positions.nuance: The ban covers facial recognition specifically; it is the closest programme measure to AI-assisted video surveillance. Votes on algorithmic video surveillance were not verified.

positions.summary: Reaffirm that fundamental principles of the (6th Republic) Constitution prevail over EU law, and refuse any EU norm less ambitious than the national norm socially or ecologically.

sources.quote: "Réaffirmer la supériorité des principes fondamentaux inscrits dans la Constitution de la 6e République sur le droit européen"

positions.nuance: This is limited to constitutional principles plus a non-regression clause, so it is narrower than general primacy of French law.

positions.summary: No evidence found on EU joint borrowing.
positions.nuance: The programme sections checked (69, 70, 49) do not address joint EU borrowing; LFI's monetary proposals focus on the ECB.

positions.summary: Make France's contribution to the EU budget conditional, as a lever in its EU strategy.

sources.quote: "Conditionner la contribution française au budget de l'Union européenne"

positions.nuance: Conditionality is a bargaining lever rather than an outright cut, so this is coded as partial support.

positions.summary: The programme counts France's veto as a key lever, which suggests opposition to removing unanimity.

sources.quote: "Utiliser le droit de veto de la France, par exemple pour refuser tout nouvel accord de libre-échange"

positions.nuance: Inferred; the veto passage concerns trade and enlargement, not foreign policy specifically.

positions.summary: An explicit strategy of disobeying EU rules (posted workers, budget, competition, capital movements) that block the programme.

sources.quote: "nous désobéirons aux règles européennes incompatibles avec l'application de l'Avenir en commun"
"appliquer notre programme quoi qu'il en coûte"

positions.summary: The 2022 programme pursues treaty change through negotiation and disobedience, with any agreement put to referendum; leaving the EU is not proposed, and the NUPES deal explicitly excluded exit.

sources.quote: "Tant qu'un accord de changement des traités n'est pas acquis, nous discutons avec nos partenaires et désobéissons aux règles bloquantes en parallèle."
Paraphrase: the NUPES agreement explicitly excluded exit from the Union, its disintegration or ending the single currency.

positions.nuance: The 2017 'Plan B' treated exit as a fallback; the 2022 programme dropped it. No 2026 statement on exit was verified.

positions.summary: On 16 Sept 2026 (LCI) Le Pen said France can no longer help Ukraine financially, while training soldiers and supplying defensive material can continue.

sources.quote: On peut continuer à former leurs soldats, leurs armées, on peut continuer à leur apporter du matériel pour pouvoir se défendre. Mais financièrement, nous ne pouvons plus.

positions.nuance: Partial support only (training, defensive material); wants reduced financial effort, framed as a public-finance constraint. Bardella (2024) also warned against weapons able to reach Russian territory. Not full opposition, hence -1.

positions.nuance: Coded from background knowledge of RN statements (2024-2025); web search budget exhausted during verification and no live source found. Needs live verification.

positions.summary: Le Pen defends leaving NATO's integrated command (2022 programme; reported again in Oct 2026 analysis), but Bardella said not while the war lasts.

On ne change pas les traités en période de guerre (Bardella)
if elected she would remove France from NATO's integrated military command

positions.nuance: Bardella (March 2024) conditioned exit on the end of the war; the 2024 RN legislative programme omits NATO exit. Le Pen's own line remains exit. +1 because of the conditionality.

positions.summary: Le Pen's 2017 programme targeted 3% of GDP for defence by 2022; RN supports higher military budgets in 2026 if they strengthen sovereignty, with no explicit 2027 figure found.

Le Rassemblement national a soutenu la hausse du budget militaire, sous réserve qu'elle renforce la souveraineté française.

positions.nuance: 3% (not above) was a 2017 target; no 2026 figure verified, and Le Pen stresses public-finance constraints (Sept 2026). Hence +1.

positions.summary: The 2017 programme proposed a compulsory 3-month military service; the 2024 RN programme only proposes experimenting a voluntary national heritage service.

sources.quote: Expérimenter la création d'un Service national volontaire du patrimoine

positions.nuance: Conflicting signals: compulsory service in 2017 (not re-verified live), only a voluntary scheme in 2024. No 2026 statement found. Coded 0 as unclear/shifted.

positions.summary: Le Pen has called sanctions on Russia useless (older statements); lifting tied to a peace deal not verified for 2026.

positions.nuance: Old source; page returned 403 during verification, so only the headline is attested. She advocates diplomacy/a peace conference. Low confidence.

Maintenir l'existence des ZFE mais les rendre facultatives - Marine Le Pen: contre
Supprimer les Zones à Faibles Emissions

sources.quote: Suppression de la hausse de 2025 des taxes sur le secteur aérien

positions.summary: RN rejects 'punitive ecology' that penalises purchasing power and growth.

sources.quote: une écologie punitive à travers des normes qui pénalisent à la fois le pouvoir d'achat et la croissance

sources.quote: Sortir des règles européennes de fixation des prix de l'énergie qui affaiblissent notre compétitivité

sources.quote: Mettre en place la priorité nationale (si nécessaire par référendum constitutionnel)

positions.nuance: Justice-referendum aspect not separately verified.

positions.summary: LFI voted against the March 2024 Assemblée vote approving the France-Ukraine security accord, which included military aid. Mélenchon has regretted EU arms deliveries since 2022. The 2027 programme stresses a ceasefire and negotiation and does not mention arms.

sources.quote: Headline (URL slug): l'Assemblée nationale vote en faveur de l'accord de sécurité franco-ukrainien, le RN et LFI s'y opposent (body not fetchable)
Je regrette que l'Union européenne ait décidé de fournir des armements nécessaires à une guerre
Paraphrase: diplomatic framework for a ceasefire, Russian troop withdrawal and peace negotiations; no arms-aid commitment.

positions.nuance: No 2025-2026 explicit statement on arms deliveries found. The Euractiv article body could not be fetched (it redirects to euractiv.com/fr, which blocks fetching), so the vote detail rests on its headline. Confidence lowered to medium for that reason.

positions.summary: Mélenchon accepts troops only as UN-commanded interposition forces and rejects the European coalition-of-the-willing format.

sources.quote: si des troupes devaient être déployées pour s'interposer et garantir la paix, elles ne pourraient l'être que sous l'autorité de l'ONU

positions.nuance: Conditional openness to a UN force, so -1 rather than -2. He opposes French deployment as currently proposed.

positions.summary: The programme pledges to leave NATO's integrated command immediately, then to leave NATO in stages.

sources.quote: Se retirer immédiatement du commandement intégré de l'OTAN puis, par étapes, de l'organisation elle-même

positions.nuance: Consistent with L'Avenir en commun 2022.

positions.summary: Mélenchon says an LFI government would suspend the EU-Israel association agreement and impose a total arms embargo.

sources.quote: L'économie d'Israël ne peut pas vivre sans l'Europe. Ils auraient été obligés d'arrêter le carnage.
Paraphrase: sanctions against the Netanyahu government with a weapons embargo.

positions.nuance: The primary statement comes from a party-aligned outlet. It is corroborated by the programme summary on a neutral site.

positions.summary: No explicit rejection of a 3% target found. He questions war-driven debt and the programme prioritises a new military programming law for sovereignty, not a spending target.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: asks whether debt for war is merely a subsidy to a capitalist economy at a dead end.

positions.nuance: No precise figure found, so coded -1 with low confidence.

positions.summary: The programme creates a mandatory nine-month 'conscription citoyenne' for women and men under 25, paid at the minimum wage, with military training (with conscientious objection) and public-service tasks.

sources.quote: Mettre en place une conscription citoyenne de neuf mois, pour les femmes et les hommes de moins de 25 ans, rémunérée au SMIC
Paraphrase: optional military service as a component of a mandatory citizen service.

positions.nuance: The statement covers compulsory military or national service. The citizen service is compulsory, while the military component allows conscientious objection or is optional.

positions.summary: In 2022 he had reservations about cutting Russia off from SWIFT and he wants a negotiated peace. The programme demands that Russian troops withdraw. No explicit statement on lifting sanctions in stages was found.

sources.quote: Le peuple russe n'est pas notre ennemi, ne le confondons pas avec le régime nationaliste
Paraphrase: framework for ceasefire, Russian troop withdrawal and peace negotiations.

positions.nuance: Mixed evidence, so coded 0.

positions.summary: The programme calls for a moratorium on low-emission zones (ZFE) in their current form because of social inequity. It does not call for outright abolition.

sources.quote: Décréter un moratoire sur les zones à faibles émissions (ZFE) dans leur conception actuelle

positions.nuance: Partial support: a moratorium and redesign, short of abolition.

positions.summary: The programme would immediately ban the most dangerous pesticides (glyphosate, neonicotinoids) and block imports of contaminated products.

sources.quote: interdire immédiatement les plus dangereux (glyphosate, néonicotinoïdes)

positions.nuance: The national ban comes with protection against imports, which fits the 'even if foreign competitors keep using them' wording.

positions.summary: Most LFI MEPs (Aubry, Chaibi, Omarjee, Pelletier) voted for the 2023 EU regulation that ends sales of new combustion cars in 2035; Mesure abstained. The programme does not mention 2035 and focuses on SUV limits and French light EV manufacturing.

sources.quote: CO2 emission standards for cars and vans - The Left group: For 26, Against 1, Abstentions 6

positions.nuance: Group and party vote from 2023. No 2025-2026 personal statement found on keeping 2035 against the planned softening. Coded +1.

positions.summary: The programme ends the tax breaks on kerosene and abolishes air routes where a train alternative takes under 4 hours.

sources.quote: Mettre fin aux niches fiscales sur le kérosène pour limiter le dumping du e-commerce depuis l'étranger
Supprimer les lignes aériennes quand l'alternative en train est inférieure à quatre heures

positions.nuance: Ending the kerosene exemption is a direct tax rise, and banning short flights goes further than taxing them. No private-jet tax measure was found in the summary.

positions.summary: The programme would put a 'règle verte' in the Constitution (take no more from nature than it can rebuild), introduce ecological planning, and replace GDP with new indicators of human progress.

sources.quote: Inscrire dans la Constitution le principe de la « règle verte »
nouveaux indicateurs de progrès humain

positions.nuance: Putting ecology ahead of growth is implied by a constitutional green rule. It is not stated as a trade-off in these words.

positions.summary: The programme would exit nuclear power and abandon EPR projects.

sources.quote: Sortir du nucléaire : abandonner les projets d'EPR

positions.nuance: None.

sources.quote: un plan d'urgence pour l'éolien maritime

positions.nuance: None.

sources.quote: Convoquer une Constituante pour passer à la 6e République

sources.quote: Élire l'Assemblée nationale au scrutin proportionnel

sources.quote: Instaurer le Référendum d'initiative citoyenne

positions.nuance: None.

positions.summary: The programme would abolish forced-vote procedures such as Article 49.3.

sources.quote: Abolir les procédures de « votes forcés » du Parlement comme l'article 49.3

positions.nuance: None.

positions.summary: The RIC as proposed would let citizens propose or repeal any law, which in principle widens referendum scope. No statement was found endorsing referendums specifically on immigration or justice, and LFI is reported to be wary of right-wing immigration referendums.

sources.quote: Instaurer le Référendum d'initiative citoyenne

positions.nuance: Coded 0: broad citizen-initiated referendums in general, but the topic-specific stance is unverified. LFI's wariness of immigration referendums was not verified in this session.

positions.summary: The programme would renationalise SNCF and stop competition on rail routes, cancel energy-market liberalisation, renationalise EDF and Engie, and reverse privatisations.

sources.quote: Annuler la libéralisation du marché de l'électricité et du gaz
Paraphrase: renationalise SNCF and prevent competition on lines

result.bio: Bruno Retailleau (born 20 November 1960 in Cholet) is a conservative politician from the Vendée, senator for Vendée (2004-2024, and again since November 2025) and president of Les Républicains since 18 May 2025. He chaired the Vendée departmental council and the Pays de la Loire regional council, led the LR group in the Senate from 2014 to 2024, and served as Interior Minister in the Barnier, Bayrou and first Lecornu governments (September 2024 - October 2025). He declared his 2027 presidential candidacy on 12 February 2026 and won the LR members' nomination on 19 April 2026. He is known for a restrictive line on immigration and security and for socially conservative positions.

result.bio: Gabriel Attal (born 16 March 1989 in Clamart) is a Renaissance politician. He was a Socialist Party member from 2006 and left it when he became Emmanuel Macron's candidate in the 2017 legislative elections. He served continuously in government from October 2018. He became France's youngest Prime Minister in January 2024 and led a caretaker government after the June 2024 dissolution until September 2024. He chairs the Ensemble pour la République group in the Assemblée nationale and has been Renaissance general secretary since December 2024. He announced his 2027 presidential candidacy on 22 May 2026 in Mur-de-Barrez (Aveyron).

delivery.what: Abaya and qamis ban in public schools (Education Minister, announced late August 2023 and applied from the September 2023 school year)
delivery.assessment: The government presented it as an application of secularism in schools. Per Wikipedia, left-wing parties and Muslim organisations contested it. No supporting or critical outlet was opened directly, so a multi-outlet balanced assessment is still missing.

delivery.what: Premiership (9 January to 16 July 2024, then caretaker until 5 September 2024)
delivery.assessment: His government had 15 members at formation and 35 after the 8 February 2024 reshuffle. Media coverage cited by Wikipedia described the line-up as a 'droitisation' (rightward shift), with several ministers who had served under Nicolas Sarkozy. Wikipedia says he disagreed with Macron's June 2024 decision to dissolve the Assemblée but still led the campaign. The Ensemble coalition won about 20% in the first round of the 2024 legislative elections. Wikipedia's article on the government has no content in its section on main actions.

The government's stated reasons (its response to farmers' protests) and any supporting outlets were not retrieved.

delivery.what: 'Choc des savoirs' (ability-level groups in collège) and school-uniform trial (Education Minister and PM, 2023-2024)
delivery.assessment: Both were launched under his authority, and the uniform trial ran in about 10 schools. Per French Wikipedia, the level groups were judged ineffective and abandoned about two years later. The uniform trial was ended in summer 2026 after showing no demonstrated effect on learning. Both decisions were taken by later governments. Neither was verified against a primary or second source.

result.bio: Raphaël Glucksmann (born 15 October 1979 in Boulogne-Billancourt) is a French essayist, documentary filmmaker and politician, son of philosopher André Glucksmann. He co-founded Place publique in 2018 and has been a Member of the European Parliament (S&D group) since 2 July 2019, leading the PS-Place publique list in 2019 (6.19%) and 2024 (13.83%, third place). He has co-led Place publique with Aurore Lalucq since 16 December 2022. On 23 August 2026 he announced his candidacy in the Socialist Party primary for the 2027 presidential election.

offices.office: Member of the European Parliament (France; S&D; Foreign Affairs committee and Human Rights subcommittee; vice-president of the Human Rights subcommittee in the 2019-2024 term; elected chair of the special committee on foreign interference on 23 September 2020)
Co-president of Place publique (with Aurore Lalucq)
Special adviser to Georgian President Mikheil Saakashvili

delivery.what: China and human-rights work in the European Parliament: focused on Xinjiang and forced labour in supply chains; sanctioned by China in 2021 (sanctions lifted April 2025); led a seven-MEP delegation to Taiwan in November 2021.

media_portrayal.left_media: Not researched at outlet level. Wikipedia records that the left-leaning outlet Le Média published (2 October 2026) the recording that triggered the September-October 2026 controversy, and that Mediapart covered the May 2026 leaked memo.
media_portrayal.right_media: Not researched: web search budget exhausted before outlet-level sources could be gathered.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Not researched at outlet level. Wikipedia notes two 2026 controversies: a campaign memo on target voter groups revealed by Politico on 12 May 2026 (he called it a stolen document with no political value; his team called it a working paper whose contested page was withdrawn), and a 17 September video published by Le Média on 2 October 2026 in which he reportedly insulted Mélenchon and Le Pen and said Ségolène Royal had done a 'danse du ventre' before Macron; Royal called the remark sexist, and he said he was sorry for 'inelegant remarks'.

result.sources_note: Only the French and English Wikipedia articles on Glucksmann could be consulted (via WebFetch summaries); the WebSearch budget (200 calls) was exhausted in both the research and the verification passes, so no AFP, franceinfo, Le Monde or Public Sénat confirmation was possible. No primary sources (programme, roll-call votes, interviews) or multi-lean press were verified. Legal list is empty because no case appears on Wikipedia, but no dedicated check against court or press sources was possible. Reversals and traits are left empty because the multi-source, different-lean rule could not be met. Wikipedia is a secondary aggregator and summaries were produced by a small model, so details need confirmation. Policy points seen on Wikipedia: declined to use the term genocide for Gaza (March 2024), refuses alliance with LFI, proposes exit from Dublin III, criticised the 2024 EU Migration and Asylum Pact, supports wealth taxation, backs Ukraine EU integration. A rerun with a raised search budget is recommended.

positions.summary: The programme calls for a large multi-year investment plan in all renewables, with regional plans that explicitly include wind.

sources.quote: Lancer un grand plan d'investissement pluriannuel dans toutes les énergies renouvelables ... soleil, vent, rivière

positions.nuance: The programme does not mention a wind moratorium, but its investment plan contradicts one.

positions.summary: The programme wants part of electricity bills based on French production costs and not on volatile market prices, but it does not propose leaving the European market.

sources.quote: Fixer une partie de la facture ... sur le coût de production de notre électricité nucléaire et renouvelable, et non plus sur un prix de marché

positions.nuance: It favours partial decoupling within the EU framework. Combined with his federalist stance, exit is unlikely.

positions.summary: The programme proposes a citizens' convention to lay the groundwork for a constituent assembly to change the Constitution, rebalancing power towards Parliament.

sources.quote: Lancer en parallèle une grande convention citoyenne qui jettera les bases d'une assemblée constituante pour changer la Constitution

positions.nuance: The programme does not use the label 'VIe République', but it pairs a new constitution with explicit parliamentary rebalancing (a PM invested by the Assembly, ending article 16).

positions.summary: The programme calls for introducing proportional representation immediately, preferably by regional constituencies.

sources.quote: Instaurer immédiatement la proportionnelle, de préférence par circonscriptions régionales

positions.summary: The programme proposes a citizens' initiative right that can trigger local and national referendums.

sources.quote: Instaurer un droit d'initiative citoyenne, permettant de déclencher des séquences démocratiques avec des référendums à l'échelle locale et nationale

positions.nuance: It does not use the term 'RIC' and the scope and binding force are unspecified, so it is coded +1.

positions.summary: The programme proposes a constructive censure motion explicitly so as to end article 49.3.

sources.quote: instaurer la motion de censure "constructive" ... ce qui permettra de mettre fin au 49.3

positions.summary: No evidence on widening referendums to immigration or justice.
positions.nuance: The programme does not address this. Search was unavailable during verification.

positions.summary: No evidence retrieved on assisted dying.
positions.nuance: The programme has no end-of-life section. Search was unavailable during verification. Priority for re-research.

positions.summary: No evidence retrieved.
positions.nuance: The programme does not address this. Search was unavailable during verification.

positions.summary: No evidence retrieved.
positions.nuance: The programme does not address this. Search was unavailable during verification.

positions.summary: The programme defends laïcité as guaranteeing freedom of conscience and worship, and proposes phasing out the derogatory regimes to the 1905 law.
positions.nuance: No explicit statement on further restricting citizens' religious expression, so not coded.

positions.summary: No evidence on surrogacy (GPA).
positions.nuance: The programme only mentions harmonising PMA laws and cross-border recognition of filiation. Nothing on GPA.

positions.summary: No evidence retrieved.
positions.nuance: The programme does not address this.

positions.summary: The programme wants fewer pupils per teacher in primary school, an experiment in secondary, and a 5-year teacher pay rise.

sources.quote: Réduire le nombre d'élèves par enseignant en primaire et l'expérimenter dans le second degré

positions.nuance: The goal matches the statement, but there is no explicit commitment to large-scale recruitment, and secondary school is limited to an experiment. Coded +1.

positions.summary: No evidence retrieved.
positions.nuance: The programme does not address ability grouping.

positions.summary: The programme proposes bringing state-contracted private schools into school catchment allocation (carte scolaire) to strengthen social mix.

sources.quote: Intégrer les établissements privés sous contrat à la carte scolaire pour garantir une répartition équitable des élèves et renforcer la mixité sociale

positions.nuance: It shares the social-mix goal but uses a different instrument (catchment areas, not funding cuts), so it is coded +1.

positions.summary: The programme proposes to 'deeply rethink' Parcoursup through consultation, not to abolish it or end selection.

sources.quote: Repenser en profondeur Parcoursup à travers une concertation réunissant parents, étudiants, universités

positions.nuance: Reforming Parcoursup instead of abolishing it amounts to partial opposition to the statement.

positions.summary: The programme says 'soutenir l'installation' (support doctors setting up practice) without saying whether this means incentives or obligations.
positions.nuance: Ambiguous, so not coded. Check his stance on the 2025 Garot bill regulating doctors' installation.

positions.summary: No evidence retrieved.
positions.nuance: The programme does not address co-payments (franchises).

positions.summary: The programme calls for rent caps in high-pressure housing zones.

sources.quote: Encadrer les loyers dans les zones en grande tension pour garantir l'accès au logement aux ménages modestes

positions.nuance: 'Zones en grande tension' corresponds closely to 'zones where housing is scarce'.

positions.summary: The programme wants to end the 'dogma of free and undistorted competition' and the competition between administrations and the private sector.

sources.quote: Mettre fin aux logiques néo-managériales qui organisent la concurrence entre administrations et avec le privé

positions.nuance: There is no explicit statement on rail or energy liberalisation, so it is coded -1 and not -2.
