positions.summary: Rejects higher taxes on wealth: says the state is poor because it spends too much, and promised to scrap the 2026 'taxe sur le patrimoine improductif' (which hit financial savings).

sources.quote: L'Etat n'est pas pauvre parce qu'il taxe trop peu – il est pauvre parce qu'il dépense trop.
Nous reviendrons sur les folies fiscales de LFI et du RN, comme la taxe sur le patrimoine improductif

positions.nuance: No verbatim 'no ISF' quote found. -2 rests on his explicit rejection of new wealth or asset taxes and of the Zucman tax (see eco2).

positions.summary: As LR president, said his party would not join any government that put the Zucman tax in its programme.

sources.quote: son parti ne participera à aucun gouvernement qui inclurait la taxe Zucman dans son programme

positions.nuance: Personal statement made as LR president during the autumn 2025 budget debates. The exact date is not given on the page.

positions.summary: The LR 'Produire plus' programme plans over 25 bn EUR of cuts to labour costs (including direct cuts to non-contributory employer contributions) and about 15 bn EUR of cuts to production taxes (C3S and CVAE abolished).

sources.quote: Plus de 25 milliards d'euros d'allègements porteront sur le coût du travail ... et une baisse directe des cotisations patronales non contributives.

positions.nuance: Party programme presented under his presidency of LR, which is his platform.

positions.summary: Backs trade 'reciprocity' clauses, a stronger and wider carbon border tax, and an EU that makes market access depend on production on its soil. Rejects 'protectionnisme de repli' and does not call for tariffs or quotas on French sectors.

sources.quote: Nous défendrons également, fermement, une Europe qui conditionne davantage l'accès à son marché à une production sur son sol.

positions.nuance: Partial support: protection works through standards, reciprocity and the CBAM, at EU level. There are no explicit national tariffs or quotas.

positions.summary: No statement found on renationalising energy or motorways.
positions.nuance: The LR electricity programme (2026) keeps EDF's current status and proposes contracts for difference, with nothing on bringing it back under public control. Nothing was found on motorways. This leans against the statement but is too indirect to code.

positions.summary: Pledges to be 'the president who lowers inheritance taxes': gifts of up to 150,000 EUR per parent to children under 30 tax-free, and no inheritance tax on family businesses while they are not sold.

sources.quote: Je ne serai pas le président qui augmentera les droits de succession mais celui qui les baissera.

positions.summary: Fiercely opposed the 2025 suspension of the reform that raised the age to 64 and pledged to reverse the suspension.

sources.quote: Bien entendu, nous supprimerons la suspension de la réforme des retraites, qui est d'une démagogie sans nom.

positions.summary: Says people will have to retire 'a bit later', taking arduous jobs into account. Gives no specific target age above 64.

sources.quote: nous ne ferons pas l'économie de partir un peu plus tard à la retraite, en prenant en compte, évidemment, la pénibilité des métiers.

positions.nuance: Supports working longer in principle without committing to an age above 64. A 23/09/2026 video ('Je veux sauver notre système de retraite') could not be transcribed.

positions.summary: The LR programme creates a funded pension tier with an individual retirement savings account for every worker, fed by profit-sharing and savings. The programme explicitly calls it 'complémentaire et volontaire'.

sources.quote: nous mettrons en place un étage de retraite fondé sur l'épargne individuelle, complémentaire et volontaire ... Un compte d'épargne retraite sera ouvert pour chaque actif.

positions.nuance: Partial support: supports a capitalisation tier 'pour tous', but it is voluntary, while the statement says mandatory. Details are deferred to a later pensions proposal.

positions.summary: Puts deficit reduction through spending cuts first: 'moins d'impôts et plus d'économies', more than 30 bn EUR of Senate savings, and a 2026 deficit target of 4.7% of GDP. Calls debt asphyxiating.

sources.quote: Le Sénat a une position raisonnable : moins d'impôts et plus d'économies. Nous voulons revenir bien en dessous de 5 %, à 4,7 % du PIB

positions.nuance: No explicit commitment to a date for getting under 3% was found. The priority on spending-led consolidation is clear.

positions.summary: Proposes not replacing any civil servant who retires.

sources.quote: En assumant, par exemple, le non-remplacement de tous les fonctionnaires qui vont partir à la retraite.

positions.summary: Rejects debt-financed spending: says debt-funded purchasing power and 'argent magique' have failed and that debt is asphyxiating France.

sources.quote: Le temps de l'argent magique est révolu. Fabriquer artificiellement du pouvoir d'achat avec de la dette ... tout cela a échoué.

positions.nuance: No quote specifically on debt for the green transition. He also attacks 'écolos bobos' who make the poor pay for the transition.

positions.summary: No statement or vote found by Retailleau on a constitutional golden rule.
positions.nuance: LR has historically backed a golden rule (2011 Sarkozy bill), but nothing from 2025-2026 or personal to him was verified.

positions.summary: In 2018 he called a fellow LR member's proposal for a sharp SMIC rise 'désolante'. His current programme raises net pay by cutting contributions, not by raising the SMIC.

sources.quote: Il qualifie également de « désolante » la forte hausse du SMIC préconisée par son homologue au sein du parti LR Guillaume Peltier

positions.nuance: The direct statement dates from 2018. The 2026 programme ('seuil zéro cotisation') offers a different way to raise pay.

positions.summary: The LR 'Travail gagnant' programme applies the June 2024 rules that shorten the maximum benefit period. It also caps payouts after a 'rupture conventionnelle' at six months and speeds up the reduction of benefits over time.

sources.quote: Elle réduit la durée maximale d'indemnisation, adapte les droits en fonction de la conjoncture et renforce les obligations de recherche d'emploi.

positions.nuance: Expected savings of about 13 bn EUR a year.

positions.summary: LR would replace the RSA with a 'Revenu d'incitation à l'activité': an unconditional 300 EUR base, plus 250 EUR on condition of at least 15 hours a week of training or job search.

sources.quote: justifiant d'au moins quinze heures d'activité hebdomadaires, son RIA est complété par un « RIA Insertion » de 250 euros par mois.

positions.nuance: Partial: activity hours condition only a top-up. The base payment carries no activity requirement.

positions.summary: Wants to 'leave the 35 hours behind' through overtime and company-level negotiation, and opposes working less. Backed 39 hours in 2019.

sources.quote: Instaurer la Priorité Travail, c'est sortir des 35 heures par le haut, avec des heures supplémentaires pour tous ceux qui le souhaitent.
En 2019, il se prononce par ailleurs pour le retour à la semaine de travail de 39 heures

positions.summary: Pledges a referendum on a law to 'drastically reduce immigration', restrictions on family reunification, and says 'l'immigration n'est pas une chance'.

sources.quote: je vous soumettrai directement par référendum plusieurs grands textes de loi : pour réduire drastiquement l'immigration

positions.summary: Promises a referendum in autumn 2027 on a constitutional pact that opens Article 11 referendums to migration policy. Also promises a referendum on a law to drastically cut immigration.

sources.quote: je soumettrai ce pacte constitutionnel à un référendum dès la rentrée 2027

positions.summary: Says the AME will be abolished and turned into emergency medical aid.

sources.quote: Nous supprimerons l'AME en la transformant en une aide médicale d'urgence.

positions.summary: As Interior Minister he ended the Valls circular to tighten regularisation of undocumented migrants. Calls mass regularisations an 'appel d'air'.

sources.quote: il déclare qu'il va mettre fin à la circulaire Valls pour durcir les conditions de régularisation des sans papiers
Les régularisations massives sont une fausse générosité et un vrai appel d'air.

positions.summary: Proposes that newly arrived foreigners prove five years of legal residence and work before receiving benefits, and that social housing go first to workers. He does not propose priority for citizens as such.

sources.quote: les nouveaux venus devront justifier de cinq ans d'activité – qui devront correspondre, évidemment, à cinq années de résidence légale
les ressortissants étrangers devront justifier de cinq années de résidence en France et d'exercice d'une activité professionnelle.

positions.nuance: Partial: a residence and work waiting period for foreigners, not national preference. He criticises Le Pen's programme as encouraging welfare dependency.

positions.summary: Wants to abolish droit du sol through a 'charte de l'ordre républicain' put to referendum.

sources.quote: Expulser tous ceux qui n'ont rien à faire en France, supprimer le droit au mariage pour les OQTF, abolir le droit du sol

positions.summary: As a senator he voted against the 2011 constitutional bill giving non-EU residents the right to vote in municipal elections.

sources.quote: Contre : ... Bruno Retailleau

positions.nuance: The vote dates from 2011. No later reversal was found, and the position is consistent with his current immigration line.

positions.summary: Wants minimum sentences made mandatory, no longer left to the judge, through a constitutional charter.

sources.quote: si aujourd'hui les peines minimales existent, leur application dépend du juge. Je veux qu'elles soient désormais obligatoires

positions.summary: Advocates lowering the age of criminal majority to 16 as part of a 'révolution pénale'.

sources.quote: l'abaissement de la majorité pénale à 16 ans et la suspension des aides sociales

positions.nuance: Secondary source, and the date of the original statement was not verified. Lowering criminal majority to 16 goes beyond the statement, which is limited to serious crimes.

positions.summary: Strong defender of the police as Interior Minister. No statement found on an independent oversight body.
positions.nuance: Inferred from his record. Downgraded from -2 because no direct evidence was found.

positions.summary: As minister he ran a February 2025 campaign aimed at making drug users feel guilty, and pursued an anti-narcotrafficking law.

sources.quote: Il fait diffuser un clip en février 2025, visant à culpabiliser les consommateurs de drogue

positions.nuance: No explicit quote on cannabis legalisation was verified. The repressive record is clear.

positions.summary: The LR AI programme would allow AI video analysis ('vidéo intelligente') in public spaces under a strict legal framework. It bans real-time facial recognition for mass surveillance.

sources.quote: nous autoriserons, dans un cadre strict et contrôlé, la vidéo intelligente pour protéger nos lieux publics et accélérer les secours.

positions.nuance: Partial: authorised with safeguards rather than 'généralisée'.

positions.summary: Wants the Constitution to rank above EU law (Article 88) and a 'constitutional shield' against European case law. EU law would still rank above ordinary statutes, and he rejects a 'Frexit juridique'.

sources.quote: remettre le droit de l'UE à sa juste place : au-dessus des lois ... mais en dessous de notre Constitution.

positions.nuance: Partial: national law prevails only at constitutional level and on competence (subsidiarity) grounds. Asked if he rejects the primacy of EU law, he answered 'Dans certains cas, oui'.

positions.summary: No evidence found on EU joint borrowing.
positions.nuance: Search budget was exhausted. The LR pages checked had nothing on the topic.

positions.summary: No evidence found on France's EU budget contribution.
positions.nuance: Not found in the LR programme pages checked.

positions.summary: No evidence found on EU foreign-policy unanimity.
positions.nuance: He says he is 'pas du tout fédéraliste', which hints at opposition but is too indirect to code.

positions.summary: Proposes that an organic law can override European case law that goes against France's fundamental interests. Also says France must keep its EU commitments.

sources.quote: je propose qu'une loi organique puisse revenir sur une jurisprudence européenne si elle est contraire à nos intérêts fondamentaux.

positions.nuance: Partial: targets court interpretations (CJEU, ECHR) beyond the treaties rather than outright non-application of EU rules. 'J'entends que la France tienne ses engagements vis-à-vis de l'UE.'

positions.summary: Explicitly rejects even a 'Frexit juridique' and wants France to stay a loyal EU partner.

sources.quote: car, sinon, c'est un Frexit juridique, que je ne souhaite pas

verification_notes: Method: the WebSearch budget for the session was exhausted (200/200), so verification used WebFetch/curl on primary sources: republicains.fr articles and programme PDFs, fr/en Wikipedia, and senat.fr roll-calls. Most draft sources were vague 'tool summaries' of the Wikipedia page and were replaced with verbatim quotes where possible.

Source lean caveat: many new sources are interviews in Le Figaro, Le Parisien, L'Opinion, JDD and La Tribune Dimanche, reproduced on the LR site, so they are labelled campaign-or-party. Corroboration from an outlet of a different lean was not possible without search.

positions.summary: Strongly pro-Ukraine: visited Kyiv and met Zelensky in May 2026, pledging to stand by Ukraine 'until the conditions for peace are met, and even beyond'. In September 2026 he clashed with Marine Le Pen over the RN's call to 'cut off' aid to Kyiv.

sources.quote: Édouard Philippe a rencontré Volodymyr Zelensky à Kyiv
determination to stand by Ukraine until peace conditions are met, and even beyond (paraphrase/translation)
« Couper le robinet à l'Ukraine » : le ton est monté entre Edouard Philippe et Marine Le Pen au sujet de l'aide à Kiev (headline)
Maintenir un soutien militaire et financier à l'Ukraine tant que nécessaire

positions.nuance: The programme wording comes from an aggregator, not the primary text. His 2026 statements and the clash with Le Pen corroborate it independently.

positions.summary: In Kyiv (May 2026) he backed deploying European troops in Ukraine once peace returns, to deter a new Russian attack. The French share is not specified.

sources.quote: favorable au déploiement de troupes européennes en Ukraine une fois la paix revenue (paraphrase)
European troops being deployed in Ukraine once peace has returned (paraphrase/translation)

positions.nuance: He backs a European, post-peace deployment, which is close to the statement but not an explicit French commitment, hence +1. Two outlets of different leans corroborate it.

positions.summary: Atlanticist: calls NATO the best security guarantee and pledged in May 2026 to work for Ukraine's entry into NATO. Leaving the integrated command is incompatible with this.

sources.quote: l'OTAN est 'la meilleure garantie de sécurité' (paraphrase)
work so that Ukraine can enter NATO (translation)
une OTAN forte c'est une Europe de la défense plus affermie

positions.nuance: The aggregator quote dates from 2018. The 2026 statements on NATO are current. He made no explicit statement on the integrated command itself.

positions.summary: Supports Israel's right to defend itself (2023). No 2025-26 statement found on suspending the EU-Israel association agreement.

sources.quote: Israël a le droit d'exister et de se défendre

positions.nuance: Inferred from 2023-era statements. A November 2023 joint call with Cazeneuve on the conflict exists but was not opened.

positions.summary: Programme as reported by an aggregator: defence budget at 3% of GDP by 2030, at the statement's threshold but not above it.

sources.quote: Porter le budget de la défense à 3 % du PIB d'ici 2030

positions.nuance: The statement asks for MORE than 3%. A 3% target is a partial version, hence +1. No primary source or press article gives a higher figure.

positions.summary: Favours expanding VOLUNTARY military service (3,000 to 50,000 places a year) and reservists. He does not propose compulsory service.

sources.quote: "Nous devons augmenter le volume de nos forces": Édouard Philippe favorable à "un service militaire volontaire" (headline)
le service militaire volontaire de 3 000 à 50 000 places par an

positions.nuance: He prefers the voluntary model but has not ruled out compulsion if circumstances change, hence -1 rather than -2.

result.bio: Éric Zemmour, born 31 August 1958 in Montreuil (Seine-Saint-Denis), is a French journalist, essayist and politician. He worked for outlets including Le Figaro, RTL, Paris Première and CNews before founding Reconquête on 5 December 2021. He finished fourth in the 2022 presidential election with 7.07% of the vote. On 17 September 2026 he said on BFMTV that he would be a candidate in 2027; his entourage said a formal declaration would follow in the autumn. Reconquête is generally classed as far-right and national-conservative, and campaigns on stopping immigration (including "remigration"), assimilation and national sovereignty in the EU.

offices.office: Legislative candidate, Var 4th constituency (3rd, 23.19%, eliminated in the first round)

legal.case: Provocation à la discrimination raciale over March 2010 remarks on France Ô (employers 'have the right to refuse Arabs or Blacks') and Canal+ 'Salut les Terriens' ('most traffickers are Black and Arab'). Tribunal correctionnel de Paris (17e chambre), suspended fine of 1,000 EUR in each of two judgments. Zemmour announced on 1 March 2011 that he would not appeal.

Provocation à la haine religieuse envers les musulmans (France 5 'C à vous', September 2016). Paris court of appeal fined him 5,000 EUR on 3 May 2018. The Cour de cassation rejected his appeal on 17 September 2019, which made the conviction final. The ECHR rejected his application on 20 December 2022.

Complicité de diffamation publique envers une administration publique (said on CNews on 2 April 2021 that INED 'manipulates' immigration figures). First-instance conviction on 29 January 2024 with a suspended fine of 1,500 EUR, upheld on appeal on 11 December 2024. The Cour de cassation rejected the appeals on 27 January 2026.

Complicité d'injure publique and provocation à la haine raciale over CNews remarks of September 2020 on unaccompanied foreign minors ('thieves, murderers, rapists'). First-instance conviction on 17 January 2022 (10,000 EUR fine), upheld by the Paris court of appeal on 12 September 2024. The Cour de cassation rejected his appeal on 2 December 2025; the penalty is 100 day-fines of 100 EUR.

Diffamation against lawyer Patrick Klugman (France 2, April 2022, Jérémie Cohen case). Convicted in January 2024 with a fine of 1,000 EUR, upheld on appeal on 5 December 2024. The Cour de cassation rejected his appeal on 2 December 2025.

Injure publique à caractère raciste against Hapsatou Sy (her first name an 'insult to France'). Tribunal de Paris on 12 January 2023 (4,000 EUR fine), upheld by the Paris court of appeal on 28 March 2024. The Cour de cassation rejected his appeal on 2 September 2025.

Injures publiques and provocation à la haine over his 28 September 2019 'Convention de la droite' speech on Muslims and immigration. Convicted at first instance on 25 September 2020 and acquitted on appeal on 8 September 2021. The Cour de cassation quashed the acquittal on 21 February 2023. At the retrial, the Paris court of appeal convicted him on 22 February 2024 (15,000 EUR fine), and the Cour de cassation rejected his appeal on 16 September 2025.

Complicité de diffamation publique against MP Danièle Obono (CNews, 2020, accused her of professing 'love for Mohamed Merah'). Tribunal correctionnel de Paris on 7 February 2024 (suspended fine of 1,000 EUR), upheld on appeal in January 2025. The Cour de cassation upheld the conviction in June 2026.

Injure raciale over remarks after the death of Thomas in Crépol (2023). Tribunal correctionnel de Paris, 9,000 EUR fine; acquitted on the 'invasion'/'Islamisation' counts. Zemmour announced an appeal. No appeal ruling was found.

Contestation de crime contre l'humanité (said on CNews in October 2019 that Pétain 'saved French Jews'). Acquitted in February 2021 and on appeal in May 2022. The Cour de cassation quashed the acquittal on 5 September 2023. At the retrial, the Paris court of appeal convicted him on 2 April 2025 (10,000 EUR fine). Zemmour announced an appeal to the Cour de cassation. No cassation ruling was found.

Contrefaçon de droit d'auteur (civil case) over unauthorised film extracts in his November 2021 candidacy video. On 4 March 2022 the tribunal judiciaire de Paris ordered Zemmour, Reconquête and the association Les Amis d'Éric Zemmour to pay 165,000 EUR in total to the rights holders. Zemmour did not appeal.
Contrefaçon de droits d'auteur (civil case, second): found liable for using extracts of Marc Aderghal's documentary 'Le Collège d'à côté' without authorisation.

Provocation à la haine ou à la violence and injure publique over CNews remarks of 2021 and March 2022 on Senegalese crack dealers. Sent to trial before the tribunal correctionnel de Paris in May 2024. No verdict was found.

Diffamation complaint by teacher Sophie Djigo over his accusations about her school trip on migration. Tried on 30-31 March 2026 alongside RN officials and acquitted in June 2026. The civil party announced an appeal.
Injures homophobes (CNews, 2019): acquitted by the Paris court of appeal in September 2024.
Preliminary investigation opened by the Paris prosecutor on 12 April 2022 into campaign SMS sent to voters identified as Jewish (complaint by UEJF and J'accuse). No later outcome was found.

delivery.what: He has held no national or local executive or legislative office. His record is electoral: 7.07% in the first round of the 2022 presidential election; 4.24% nationally for Reconquête and its allies in the 2022 legislative elections, with no candidate reaching the second round (Zemmour himself was eliminated in Var's 4th constituency with 23.19%); and 5.47% (5 MEPs) for the Reconquête list led by Marion Maréchal in the 2024 European elections.
delivery.assessment: Founded and still leads Reconquête, which has run in every national election since 2022. Its only seats are in the European Parliament. In June 2024 Zemmour expelled four of the five MEPs elected in 2024 (Marion Maréchal, Nicolas Bay, Guillaume Peltier, Laurence Trochu) after they backed the RN-Ciotti alliance for the snap legislative elections, leaving Sarah Knafo as the party's only MEP. This assessment rests on encyclopaedic sources only; no multi-lean evaluation of his impact was verified.

media_portrayal.left_media: Left-leaning outlets such as Mediapart and Libération focus heavily on his court cases; Mediapart framed the June 2026 Obono ruling as the 'latest sanction in a long list'. They also describe Reconquête as far-right. This is based on a small sample of headlines.
media_portrayal.right_media: Right-leaning outlets such as the JDD cover him mainly as a campaign and strategy story; for example, 'Éric Zemmour lance la saison 2 de sa quête de l'Élysée' (September 2026) stresses his 2027 project and Sarah Knafo's role. This is based on a single verified headline, so the characterisation is tentative.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Institutional and wire outlets (AFP via RTL, BFMTV, La Croix, franceinfo, Le Figaro) report his convictions and appeals factually with court dates and penalties. They describe him as the leader of a far-right party who has hardened his line on immigration for 2027.

result.sources_note: This verification pass used the full French Wikipedia text (as of October 2026) for the case history, and confirmed the key rulings against outlets of different leanings. Centre/neutral: franceinfo, AFP via RTL, BFMTV, La Croix, France 24, Le Club des Juristes and the Cour de cassation website. Centre-right: Le Figaro. Centre-left: HuffPost. Left: Mediapart. Right: JDD. Also used: ActuaLitté, Le Dauphiné and La Provence. Le Monde, Libération, Le Point and Ouest-France pages blocked fetching and are not cited. Reversals and traits remain empty because no multi-lean sourcing was gathered. Wikipedia lists further acquittals (2008, 2014 x2, 2016, 2017, 2019, 2022 x3) and older pending complaints (L214 diffamation, 2020 LGBT associations complaint) that are not itemised here.

result.bio: Olivier Faure (born 18 August 1968 in La Tronche, Isère) is a French Socialist politician and has been deputy for Seine-et-Marne's 11th constituency since June 2012. He has led the Parti socialiste as First Secretary since April 2018 and was re-elected in 2021, January 2023 and June 2025, the last two times narrowly. He backed the NUPES alliance in 2022 and the Nouveau Front populaire in 2024, and argues for a single candidate of the left in 2027. On 30 August 2026 he announced he would run in the socialist primary for the 2027 presidential election, and in September 2026 he published the book "La loi du plus juste".

reversals.topic: Use of article 49.3 for the 2026 budget
reversals.before: The PS had opposed the government's use of article 49.3 to pass texts without a vote (paraphrase; the Wikipedia source does not give a dated statement by Faure himself).
reversals.after: At the end of January 2026 he agreed to let the Lecornu government use 49.3 to adopt the 2026 budget, since no majority could be found. Wikipedia: 'il finit par accepter fin janvier 2026'. Other left parties opposed this.

delivery.what: As a deputy, got an amendment adopted to the finance bill (December 2014) that funded a single-price Pass Navigo in Ile-de-France by raising the transport levy paid by employers
delivery.assessment: Attested only by the French Wikipedia article, which cites no outlet for this sentence. It has not been independently assessed, and the cost to businesses has not been evaluated.

delivery.what: Kept the PS inside left alliances: NUPES in 2022, the NFP in 2024, and a push for a common left candidacy for 2027
delivery.assessment: Supporters credit him with keeping the PS in a union strategy. According to Wikipedia, many PS figures accuse him of 'subordination' to Jean-Luc Melenchon. Only Wikipedia was consulted, so no sources of different leanings were checked.

delivery.what: Negotiated with PM Lecornu a suspension of the 2023 pension reform (November 2025)
delivery.assessment: This is a concession the PS won from the government while in opposition. Other left parties criticised it as falling short of repeal. The specific terms, such as the frozen age and end date in the draft, were not confirmed in the fetched source. No sources of different leanings were obtained.

result.sources_note: Both the draft and this verification pass rely only on the French Wikipedia article on Olivier Faure. In verification, the WebSearch budget was already spent (200 of 200 calls), so AFP, franceinfo, Le Monde and Public Sénat could not be checked. Wikipedia is a secondary source with no lean label. Its sentences on the Pass Navigo amendment, the 49.3 decision and the Cazeneuve episode carry no outlet citation in the fetched text. The legal list is empty because neither the draft nor this check found any case. Absence of cases is not confirmed. Executive experience is 0 because no ministerial, mayoral or regional/departmental executive office appears in the source. The arithmetic is correct given that. Traits and media portrayal are empty or unresearched because the two-leanings bar could not be met. The proposals in 'La loi du plus juste' (regularising undocumented workers, an AI levy for pensions, SMIC at 1,700 euros) come from Wikipedia and were not re-verified. A rerun with a higher search limit is strongly recommended before publication.

positions.nuance: The party supported the tax in 2025, citing RTL of 11 September 2025. No personal 2026 statement by Glucksmann endorsing the 2% / EUR 100m design was found. Search tools were exhausted, so a personal 2025 statement may exist and could not be confirmed.

positions.summary: He wants to redirect what he calls the 211bn of tax breaks and exemptions for firms, and to cut employee CSG rather than employer charges. The programme scraps 'inefficient' tax advantages for large firms.

sources.quote: Il y a par exemple 211 milliards de cadeaux fiscaux ou d'exonération pour les entreprises. ... On va les réorienter
Sa proposition : baisser « la CSG sur les salaires pour les salariés »

positions.nuance: He does not explicitly reject every cut to production taxes. His line is to reorient and condition business aid rather than add new cuts, so this is partial opposition.

positions.summary: The programme calls for 'targeted, intelligent protectionism', customs barriers against Chinese competition, trade-defence safeguard clauses and a Buy European Act. His August 2026 letter says 'we will protect our productions'.

sources.quote: bâtir un protectionnisme ciblé et intelligent ... protégerons les entreprises européennes de la concurrence chinoise par des barrières douanières
Nous protégerons nos productions et nous remettrons des usines dans nos territoires.

positions.nuance: The protection is framed at European level (EU tariffs, Buy European Act) rather than French-only. He does not explicitly accept that prices may rise.

positions.summary: The programme favours public steering of industry and regional stakes in key firms. It also proposes rethinking the motorway system and redirecting toll revenue, but makes no explicit renationalisation pledge for energy or motorways.

sources.quote: Repenser le système autoroutier ... affecter les recettes de péage à la mobilité durable

positions.nuance: No explicit call to bring energy or motorways back under public ownership was found. This is an inference from his interventionist industrial line.

positions.summary: He campaigns on raising taxes on 'mega-inheritances' to fund wage increases. That is the opposite of lowering inheritance taxes.

sources.quote: On est en train de devenir une société de rentiers et d'héritiers. ... Donc on taxe les méga-héritages
impasse injuste qui favorise les héritiers ou les retraités aisés aux détriments des travailleurs

positions.nuance: The proposal targets very large inheritances. No position was found on small or middle-sized estates.

positions.summary: He wants to abrogate the 2023 reform, which would restore 62, and said so at the Medef debate. He also refuses to focus on the legal age and says some people will have to work longer.

sources.quote: Abroger la réforme Macron de 2023. ... certains doivent pouvoir partir à la retraite à 60 ans, d'autres devront travailler davantage.
« Nous l'abrogerons, cette réforme, parce que nous pensons qu'elle est injuste »

positions.nuance: Abrogation mechanically restores 62, but he says the system 'doit être réformé' around arduousness and life expectancy and does not commit to 62 as a goal. Hence partial support.

positions.summary: He opposes the 64 reform and wants to stop focusing on the legal age. He nonetheless says some people will have to work longer to balance the system.

sources.quote: Le candidat à la primaire socialiste estime néanmoins que certains Français vont devoir travailler plus longtemps.
cesser la focalisation sur le seul âge légal

positions.nuance: He is against raising the legal age above 64, but he accepts longer careers for some workers based on arduousness and life expectancy, so this is not a full -2.

positions.summary: No position on mandatory capitalisation was found. The programme calls the pay-as-you-go system a 'national treasure' to be preserved.

sources.quote: Notre système de retraites, pilier de la solidarité entre générations, est un trésor national. Nous nous engageons à le préserver.

positions.nuance: Inferred. Capitalisation is not mentioned in Acte I.

positions.summary: He wants a credible deleveraging path, but through a mix of targeted savings and new revenue, together with strategic reinvestment. He does not accept large spending cuts.

sources.quote: Notre stratégie s'appuiera sur un mix responsable d'économies ciblées et de recettes nouvelles
il propose aussi d'investir massivement dans l'école, la défense ... mais souhaite dans le même temps réduire la dette et les déficits

positions.nuance: He agrees that deficits must come down, but rejects 'at the cost of large spending cuts'. No 3% deadline was found.

positions.summary: The programme pledges to support and revalue civil servants, and he wants more resources for schools and hospitals. No explicit position on headcount was found.

sources.quote: Soutenir les fonctionnaires, revaloriser durablement les rémunérations pour renforcer l'attractivité de la fonction publique

positions.nuance: Inferred from his pay and service-investment pledges. He does not explicitly reject headcount cuts, and the programme mentions state 'train de vie' savings.

positions.summary: His position is mixed. He backs large EU joint borrowing for defence and strategic reinvestment, but nationally he wants a 'credible deleveraging path' and avoiding 'l'aggravation de la dette'.

sources.quote: Assainir durablement les finances publiques par une trajectoire crédible de désendettement
en évitant « la casse du modèle social » ainsi que « l'aggravation de la dette »

positions.nuance: He accepts European debt for defence, climate and industry, and justifies investment by saying 'the cost of inaction would be heavier'. Nationally he wants debt to fall.

positions.summary: No statement found on a constitutional deficit 'golden rule'.
positions.nuance: Not mentioned in Acte I or the 2026 franceinfo coverage reviewed. A brief search was attempted but the web-search quota was exhausted.

positions.summary: The programme raises the SMIC to EUR 1,600 net within two years of taking office, about +10%, well above expected inflation. In 2026 debates he also proposes cutting employee CSG to raise take-home pay.

sources.quote: Augmenter le SMIC à 1600 euros net dans les deux ans qui suivent notre accession au pouvoir.
les cinq candidats ont rappelé leur volonté d'augmenter le smic ... en baissant la CSG (Raphaël Glucksmann)

positions.nuance: Part of the net increase may come through a CSG cut rather than the gross SMIC. The EUR 1,600 net target is more modest than the Ecologists' EUR 2,000 gross.

positions.summary: The programme pledges to repeal Macron's unemployment-insurance reform, calling it unjust and ineffective.

sources.quote: Abroger la réforme Macron de l'assurance chômage, injuste et inefficace.

positions.nuance: The programme also proposes a job guarantee (generalising 'Territoires zéro chômeur').

positions.summary: No position on mandatory RSA activity hours was found. The programme favours a single minimum income open to under-25s and a job guarantee.

sources.quote: Ouvrir une grande conférence sociale pour aller vers un minimum social unique, accessible à toutes et tous, y compris pour les moins de 25 ans

positions.nuance: Inferred. RSA conditionality is not addressed.

positions.summary: No statement found on reducing weekly working time towards 32 hours.
positions.nuance: The programme does not mention working-time reduction. The draft's -1 rested only on his not being a known 32-hour advocate, which is not evidence.

positions.summary: He wants to repeal the 2024 immigration law, create legal and safe labour-migration routes, and use legal labour immigration to raise the number of pension contributors.

sources.quote: Créer des voies légales et sécurisées d'immigration de travail
Il défend la création de voies d'immigration légales en Europe, proposant le développement de quotas, basés sur les besoins économiques des États

positions.nuance: He also calls for a 'realistic and coherent' regulation of immigration (L'Opinion via franceinfo, Aug 2026) and for enforcing OQTF orders that are issued.

positions.summary: No position on an immigration referendum was found. The programme backs local and national referendums and citizens' conventions in general.
positions.nuance: Inferred from his opposition to the RN agenda. His general support for referendums makes this uncertain.

positions.summary: The 2024 NFP programme, which Place publique signed, guaranteed access to AME. No personal 2025-2026 statement was found.

sources.quote: Garantie de l'accès à l'aide médicale d'État (AME, contre les lois abrogées)

positions.nuance: This is the party line from the 2024 NFP accord, which Glucksmann has since distanced himself from. AME is absent from Acte I.

positions.summary: The programme pledges to make regularisation easier for undocumented workers and to allow asylum seekers to work as soon as their claim is registered.

sources.quote: Faciliter les démarches de régularisation des travailleurs sans papiers

positions.nuance: The pledge is broader than shortage occupations only. It is framed as easing procedures rather than mass regularisation.

positions.summary: He opposes the RN agenda that blames immigrants. No explicit statement on national preference for housing or benefits was found.

sources.quote: « Quand on vous pose la question de la dette, vous répondez 'les immigrés et l'Europe' », attaque-t-il.

positions.nuance: National preference conflicts with the equal-rights framing of the programme. The wording of this specific statement was not addressed directly.

positions.summary: Opposes abolishing droit du sol, in line with the left.
positions.nuance: No personal statement was retrieved. This is party line.

positions.summary: The programme explicitly opens the right to vote in local elections to non-EU foreigners.

sources.quote: Ouvrir le droit de vote à 16 ans et pour les étrangers extra-communautaires aux élections locales

positions.nuance: Written programme of his own party, March 2026.

positions.summary: The left opposes peines planchers. The programme stresses prevention and rejects 'coups de menton'.
positions.nuance: No explicit personal statement on mandatory minimums was found. Acte I talks of 'adaptation des réponses pénales' without detail.

positions.summary: Inferred opposition. The programme emphasises early prevention for young people.
positions.nuance: No explicit statement found.

positions.summary: The programme wants to overhaul the doctrine of public-order policing and generalise receipts for ID checks. No explicit independent police-oversight body was found.

sources.quote: Généraliser les récépissés de contrôle d'identité.

positions.nuance: Adjacent police-accountability measures are present, but not an independent body replacing the IGPN.

positions.summary: He neither backs nor rejects legalisation. The programme leaves the question to a citizens' convention on drug policy.

sources.quote: Organiser une convention citoyenne sur la politique vis-à-vis des drogues, notamment la question de la légalisation du cannabis.

positions.nuance: Explicitly undecided: he defers to a citizens' convention.

positions.summary: He voted for the EU AI Act in 2023 and 2024. The Act restricts real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces.

sources.quote: Artificial Intelligence Act - Accord provisoire: Glucksmann FOR (from API record)

positions.nuance: The AI Act also allows exceptions, so supporting it is only an indirect signal against generalised AI video surveillance. No direct French statement on algorithmic video surveillance (VSA) was found.

positions.summary: A self-declared European federalist. His programme seeks a federal 'bond en avant', which is incompatible with giving French law precedence over EU law.

sources.quote: notre ambition fédérale pour l'Europe est donc guidée par le souci de l'efficacité et du réalisme

positions.nuance: No explicit statement on primacy of law was found. This is a strong inference from his federalism.

positions.summary: He wants a EUR 500bn European defence fund financed by common borrowing. This updates his 2024 proposal of a EUR 100bn fund.

sources.quote: Oeuvrer à la mise en place rapide d'un fonds européen de défense de 500 milliards d'euros via un emprunt commun.
création d'un fonds de défense de 100 milliards d'euros, financé par un nouvel emprunt européen

positions.nuance: The figure rose from EUR 100bn in the 2024 European campaign to EUR 500bn in 2026.

positions.summary: He wants a massive increase in the EU budget and new own resources, which is the opposite of cutting France's contribution. He also attacked Le Pen for targeting the EU contribution.

sources.quote: Augmenter massivement le budget de l'Union ... et attribuer à l'Union des ressources propres nouvelles.

positions.nuance: New own resources could in principle reduce national contributions, but his clear thrust is a bigger EU budget.

positions.summary: The programme proposes a treaty moving the European Council to qualified majority voting.

sources.quote: passant à la majorité qualifiée au Conseil européen

positions.nuance: Framed as general QMV in the European Council through a 2030 refoundation treaty, which covers foreign policy.

positions.summary: Inferred opposition to unilaterally disapplying EU rules, given his federalism. He does want to change some EU rules, such as revisiting 'free and undistorted competition'.

sources.quote: Revenir sur le dogme de la concurrence libre et non faussée

positions.nuance: He seeks change through EU reform, not disobedience. No explicit statement was found.

positions.summary: Strongly pro-EU and federalist. He wants France to be 'the locomotive of a sovereign Europe'.

sources.quote: Nous ferons de la France la locomotive de la puissance européenne naissante.

positions.nuance: Unambiguous.

result.bio: Marine Tondelier (born 23 August 1986, Bois-Bernard, Pas-de-Calais) has been National Secretary of EELV / Les Écologistes since 10 December 2022 and was re-elected on 19 April 2025. She was a municipal opposition councillor in Hénin-Beaumont from 2014 to March 2026 and has been a Hauts-de-France regional councillor since 2021. She announced her 2027 presidential candidacy on 22 October 2025 and was designated by her party in December 2025 to run in a planned left-wing primary. That primary did not take place. In September 2026 her party's federal council kept her as its candidate until a members' vote on 10-13 December 2026, which will decide between a standalone run and backing another left-wing candidate.

legal.case: Defamation suit brought by Hénin-Beaumont mayor Steeve Briois, Bruno Bilde and former city services director Laurent Morel (RN side) over her 2017 book 'Nouvelles du Front'; she was the defendant. The Paris correctional court found the statements defamatory but acquitted her and her publisher on grounds of good faith. The plaintiffs announced they would appeal; no appeal ruling was found.

reversals.topic: Leaving the social network X (minor; a personal and party-communication stance, not a policy)
reversals.before: On 19 November 2024 she called X 'a source of suffering' and called for it to be regulated or even shut down in France (BFM TV). On 12 January 2025 she called on the whole left to leave X.
reversals.after: On 20 January 2025 she said she would stay on X to defend ecology on 'hostile terrain', noting that most parliamentarians had not left.

result.bio: François Ruffin, born 18 October 1975 in Calais, is a journalist, documentary maker, essayist and politician. He founded the local newspaper Fakir in 1999 and directed the documentary Merci patron! (2016), which won the César for best documentary in 2017. He has been deputy for the Somme's 1st constituency since 2017 and sat with the LFI group without formally joining the party until he broke with Jean-Luc Mélenchon in July 2024; he now sits with the Écologiste et social group. He became president of Debout ! (formerly Picardie debout !) on 28 June 2025 and on 26 January 2026 announced he would stand in a left-wing primary for 2027; according to Wikipedia that primary was later cancelled, and Debout ! said that in that case it would put him forward directly for the presidential election.

offices.office: Deputy for Somme, 1st constituency (elected 2017, re-elected 2022 and 2024)
Secretary of the Economic Affairs Commission, Assemblée nationale

legal.case: Defamation over his book Quartier Nord (about residents of an Amiens neighbourhood), after a complaint by a resident. Wikipedia: 'condamné pour diffamation par le tribunal d'Amiens'. The penalty, the kind of procedure and any appeal are not stated, and no appeal has been reported since.

Ruffin as victim and civil party, not accused: in the LVMH espionage case, former intelligence chief Bernard Squarcini (Kyrnos, paid by LVMH) was tried in Nov 2024, partly over the surveillance and infiltration of Ruffin and Fakir around Merci patron!. On 7 March 2025 Squarcini was convicted at first instance and sentenced to 4 years (2 without suspension), a EUR 200,000 fine and a 5-year professional ban. His lawyers announced an appeal. Bernard Arnault denied any involvement.
HATVP stated that his audiovisual production company (non-profit) was undervalued by EUR 431,973 in his declaration. This is an administrative observation, and no proceedings are reported.

delivery.what: As a deputy since 2017 he has tabled a high volume of amendments (about 4,100 according to Wikipedia, nearly all rejected), and few of his own bills have been passed. He keeps roughly a SMIC-level income from his parliamentary pay and passes on the rest, and he gives his share of public party funding (about EUR 37,000 a year) to the PCF.

In the current legislature, datan.fr shows 88% participation in solemn votes (the average for all deputies is 89%) and 98% loyalty to the ECOS group. No assessment from outlets of different leanings was obtained.

result.bio: Jean-Luc Mélenchon is a French politician born in 1951. He spent about thirty years in the Socialist Party, serving as senator for Essonne and as junior minister for vocational education (2000-2002), left the PS in 2008 to co-found the Parti de Gauche, and founded La France insoumise (LFI) in 2016. He was an MEP from 2009 to 2017 and deputy for Bouches-du-Rhône from 2017 to 2022, and ran for president in 2012 (fourth), 2017 (fourth) and 2022 (third). On 3 May 2026 he announced a fourth candidacy for 2027, built on an updated L'Avenir en commun and a Sixth Republic via a constituent assembly.

offices.office: Conseiller général de l'Essonne and président délégué du conseil général (not president)
Ministre délégué à l'Enseignement professionnel (gouvernement Jospin), 27 March 2000 - 6 May 2002
Président du groupe LFI à l'Assemblée nationale
Co-founder of the Parti de Gauche (2008); founder and leader of La France insoumise

legal.case: Rebellion, provocation and intimidation of judicial authority during the 16 October 2018 searches of LFI headquarters: tried in Bobigny on 19-20 September 2019 and sentenced on 9 December 2019 to 3 months' suspended imprisonment and an 8,000 EUR fine. He did not appeal, so the conviction is final.

European Parliament assistants affair (suspected use of EP-paid assistants for the Parti de Gauche, 2009-2017; preliminary inquiry July 2017, judicial investigation from November 2018). Investigating judges closed the instruction on 26 May 2026 without placing Mélenchon under formal investigation (no mise en examen). Two former assistants were témoins assistés. Telos reports that no evidence established his direct involvement or an organised scheme. No formal non-lieu order was located in this check, but with no one mis en examen no trial can follow.

reversals.before: 1992: called for a yes vote on the Maastricht treaty, calling it a 'compromis de gauche' and presenting the single currency as an instrument of European civilisation.
reversals.after: Campaigned against the 2005 constitutional treaty and later said 'ce sont les opposants à ce traité qui avaient raison'. Now proposes 'Plan A / Plan B' (renegotiate the treaties or disobey them), described as 'ni Frexit, ni Europe libérale'.

reversals.before: 2014: called the annexation of Crimea 'absolutely predictable' and opposed sanctions on Russia.
reversals.after: February 2022: condemned the Russian invasion while still assigning NATO a share of responsibility; by June 2022 he endorsed arms deliveries, affirming Ukraine's right to defend itself, while opposing deeper French military involvement.

delivery.what: Junior minister for vocational education (2000-2002): reformed vocational aptitude certificates (CAP) and the validation of acquired experience (validation des acquis), and created the 'lycée des métiers' label.
delivery.assessment: Encyclopedic sources credit him with concrete reforms in a junior portfolio. The record is short (about two years) and dated, and no sources of other leanings were consulted on its impact.

delivery.what: Led the LFI group in the Assemblée nationale (June 2017 - October 2021) and built the NUPES left alliance for the 2022 legislative elections (131 seats per French Wikipedia; totals vary with how allied deputies are counted). LFI later took part in the 2024 Nouveau Front populaire, which won a relative majority; LFI proposed his name for Matignon, but the other coalition partners rejected it.
delivery.assessment: A significant coalition-building and opposition record, though he gained no executive power. Roll-call votes were not checked.

delivery.what: 2027 programme (updated L'Avenir en commun): net SMIC of 1,600 EUR, retirement at 60 after 40 years of contributions, price freezes on essential goods and energy, a strengthened wealth tax (ISF), a Sixth Republic via a constituent assembly, and a nuclear exit by 2050.
delivery.assessment: These are promises only, taken from a secondary aggregator summary and not from the primary programme text. Costings are disputed, and that dispute was not verified here.

media_portrayal.left_media: Not directly sampled in this check. LFI and sympathetic outlets present him as the main voice of social rupture and ecological planning, and present the judicial cases as political harassment. After the May 2026 closure, LFI said that no investigating judge had found grounds for a mise en examen.
media_portrayal.right_media: Right-leaning outlets (JDD, CNews) cover him largely through his legal cases and the 2018 searches. They reported the May 2026 closure of the assistants investigation without indictment.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Neutral and encyclopedic sources (Wikipedia, Telos, L'Essentiel) describe a left-wing leader with a long PS career. They mention both his oratorical talent and controversies over provocative statements, and report that he was never charged in the EP assistants case.

result.sources_note: Original research and this verification both hit the 200-search WebSearch cap. The check therefore used direct fetches of French and English Wikipedia (including the French wikitext through the Wikipedia API), L'Essentiel, JDD, Telos and the aggregator pages. CNews returned 403 and could not be confirmed. No primary court releases, AFP, franceinfo or Le Monde pages could be opened, and the French Wikipedia statement that he did not appeal the 2019 judgment is cited to secondary press there. Not consulted: roll-call votes (datan/nosdeputes), the primary programme text, and left-leaning outlets (Libération, Mediapart, L'Humanité). Lean coverage is skewed to neutral and right sources. Aggregators (testpolitique, elyseescope, monvote2027) are secondary and of uncertain lean. Treat delivery and media_portrayal as provisional.

result.bio: Marine Le Pen (born 1968) is a French lawyer-turned-politician who led the Front national, renamed Rassemblement national (RN) in 2018, from 2011 to 2021. She reached the presidential runoff in 2017 and 2022, and has been deputy for Pas-de-Calais since 2017 and chair of the RN group in the Assemblée nationale since 2022. She was convicted at first instance in March 2025 and on appeal on 7 July 2026 in the European Parliament assistants case; a cassation appeal is pending, so the conviction is not final. In July 2026 she confirmed she will run for president a fourth time, and Jordan Bardella, who had been prepared as the alternative RN candidate, stood aside.

offices.office: President of the Front national / Rassemblement national
Co-president, Europe of Nations and Freedom group (European Parliament)
Departmental councillor, Pas-de-Calais (mandate ended following the ineligibility penalty)
President of the RN group, Assemblée nationale

legal.case: European Parliament parliamentary assistants case (embezzlement of EU public funds, 2004-2016). First instance, 31 March 2025: 4 years' prison (2 firm), EUR 100,000 fine and 5 years' ineligibility with provisional (immediate) execution. Appeal, 7 July 2026: 3 years' prison of which 2 suspended (1 firm year to be served under electronic monitoring), as reported by Public Sénat and Toute l'Europe; Wikipedia gives '1 year firm + 3 years suspended', so the exact total is reported inconsistently. EUR 100,000 fine. 45 months' ineligibility, of which 30 suspended; the 15 firm months were treated as already served (to 30 June 2026), so she is eligible in 2027. Co-defendants on appeal include Louis Aliot (1 year suspended), Bruno Gollnisch (3 years suspended) and Julien Odoul (8 months suspended); Public Sénat reports the RN was fined EUR 2 million (EUR 1 million suspended). She has filed a cassation appeal. On 8 July 2026 the Court of Cassation said it 'could' rule 'au plus tard début avril 2027', a timetable it says may change; the first round is on 18 April 2027. The conviction is therefore not final.

Prosecution for incitement to hatred over a December 2010 Lyon speech comparing street prayers to an 'occupation'. The Lyon court acquitted her, ruling that the statement did not target the whole Muslim community.

reversals.before: 2017 campaign: proposed leaving the euro and restoring a national currency (Euronews: 'The euro is the currency of the bankers, not the people').
reversals.after: Late in the 2017 campaign she softened this to a 'common currency' for large firms only. By 2022 she had dropped euro exit from her programme.

reversals.before: 2017: visited Moscow and met Putin, called sanctions 'profoundly unjust and counterproductive' and proposed lifting them; defended the 2014 Crimea referendum.
reversals.after: Since February 2022 she condemns the invasion 'without ambiguity', and in 2026 the RN denounced Russian 'hostile acts' in Europe. She still opposes further financial aid to Ukraine on budget grounds and defended the Crimea referendum again in 2023, so the shift is partial.

delivery.what: She has held no national or local executive office. Her record is legislative and party-building: she has led the RN group since 2022, which became the largest single-party group in the Assemblée (about 120+ deputies) after the 2024 elections. As party leader she ran the 'dédiabolisation' strategy, including expelling her father and renaming the FN as RN in 2018.
delivery.assessment: Sources cited by Wikipedia (Le Monde, Politico Europe, New Statesman, The Conversation) describe dédiabolisation as a deliberate normalisation strategy. Critics see it as cosmetic, while supporters credit it with mainstreaming the party. A roll-call vote analysis (datan.fr, nosdeputes.fr) was not retrieved.

delivery.what: 2027 platform (positions announced so far): return to retirement at 62, or 60 for people who started work before 20 (reaffirmed August 2026). Reported continuing themes from earlier platforms include national preference in benefits and social housing, tax cuts and expulsion of foreign offenders. The full 2027 programme was not reviewed.
delivery.assessment: Le Pen costs the pension measure at about EUR 9 billion a year. Institut Montaigne (centre-right/liberal) estimates EUR 26.5 billion, or up to EUR 38 billion. France 24 carries a critical op-ed calling the platform's financing unexplained. Bardella has floated a different pension approach (no age floor, a capitalisation pillar), so the party line is not fully settled.

traits.trait: Strategic party manager focused on normalising the party's image ('dédiabolisation')
traits.evidence: Le Monde, Politico Europe, New Statesman and The Conversation (cited in Wikipedia) describe her expelling her father and renaming the party in 2018 as a deliberate normalisation strategy.

media_portrayal.left_media: Left-leaning outlets typically present her as the leader of a far-right party whose normalisation is mainly a matter of image. They foreground the embezzlement conviction, her past ties to Russia and the national-preference proposal. This is inferred from general patterns, as Libération, Mediapart and L'Humanité were not opened.
media_portrayal.right_media: Right-leaning outlets typically present her as a legitimate sovereigntist leader. They tend to frame the prosecution as politicised and to emphasise her immigration, security and purchasing-power proposals. This is inferred, as CNews and Europe 1 pages could not be opened (HTTP 403).
media_portrayal.neutral_media: France 24, franceinfo, LCP and Public Sénat report the verdict, the sentence and her eligibility in procedural detail and stress the uncertainty before the cassation ruling. They treat the Le Pen/Bardella arrangement as a strategic question for the RN.

result.sources_note: Verified in this session against Public Sénat, LCP, franceinfo, Toute l'Europe, France 24, Le Grand Continent, Euronews, Infobae, Journal du Net, Référence Entreprise, and French and English Wikipedia. positions.summary: Opposes restoring the ISF. His 2017-2020 government replaced the ISF with the IFI plus flat tax, and he defends keeping that framework.

refus du rétablissement de l'ISF

sec1: replaced the paraphrased source with the verbatim programme text, which covers the 'infractions les plus graves' rather than repeat offenders. Kept the aggregator's recidivist claim as a second source. Code +2 medium unchanged.
sec2: evidence_type statement -> vote: the evidence is the Horizons group's unanimous support for the 2025 law. Code unchanged.
sec5: +1 low record_in_office -> +1 medium programme: the 2026 programme proposes 'l'utilisation ciblée de la reconnaissance faciale' under a narco state of emergency.
eu1: removed the unverified claim about ECHR derogation from the summary. Null unchanged.
eu6: added the France-Vote 'Europe puissance' source to back up the undated quote. Code unchanged.
eco6: kept null. presi2027's 'plutôt pour' is explicitly an estimate with no measure; opposing tax increases is not the same as proposing cuts.
Confirmed without change: eco1, ret1, ret2, ret3 (LCP 29 Sept 2026, capitalisation not mandatory), fin4, trav1, trav4, sec3, sec4, eco4, eco5, eu5.

positions.summary: Le Pen proposes to abolish the real-estate IFI and replace it with a tax on financial wealth (impot sur la fortune financiere, IFF) at the same EUR 1.3m threshold. She does not back a classic ISF.

sources.quote: Marine Le Pen propose de supprimer l'IFI (qui pèse sur l'immobilier) et de le remplacer par un impôt sur la fortune financière
Paraphrase: RN abstained on restoring the ISF in 2022 and voted against restoring it in 2024; proposes replacing IFI with an IFF at the same EUR 1.3m threshold.

positions.nuance: Partial support (+1): she backs a wealth tax on financial assets but drops real estate, and the RN voted against restoring the ISF in 2024. Only secondary aggregators were checked; the RN's own text was not opened.

positions.summary: The RN group voted against the Zucman tax in the 2026 budget debate (amendments rejected 172 to 228) while promoting its own financial-wealth tax.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: amendments rejected 172 to 228; the ex-majority groups, LR and the Rassemblement national opposed them.

positions.nuance: Coded -1 rather than -2 because the RN backs a different tax on financial fortunes. It opposes the Zucman design itself. A -2 coding would also be defensible.

positions.summary: Proposes exempting employers from contributions on wage rises of up to 10% for 5 years (for wages under 3x SMIC), and abolishing the CVAE production tax.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: employer contribution exemption on wage rises up to 10% for 5 years; abolition of the CVAE.

positions.nuance: Cuts to contributions are targeted, tied to wage rises, and not a general competitiveness cut, so coded +1. The aggregator appears to draw partly on the 2022 programme.

positions.summary: Opposes free-trade agreements and promotes protectionist 'economic patriotism' and national preference in public procurement.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: against liberalisation agreements; proposes 'economic patriotism'.

positions.nuance: Tariffs and quotas are not always explicit. The RN stresses 'intelligent protectionism' and border adjustments, so coded +1 rather than +2.

positions.summary: Supports renationalising motorway concessions (cutting tolls by about 15%) and nationalising EDF to keep electricity production under state control.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: renationalise highway concessions to cut tolls 15%; backs EDF nationalisation to ensure state control of electricity production.

positions.nuance: Both sectors named in the statement are covered by explicit public-control proposals. Aggregator source only.

positions.summary: Proposes abolishing direct inheritance duties for modest and middle-class families, and exempting parental gifts of up to EUR 100,000 per child every ten years.

sources.quote: supprimer les droits de succession directs pour les modestes et classes moyennes, et creer une exemption pour les donations de parents a enfants jusqu'a 100 000 euros

positions.nuance: The cut targets modest and middle-class estates, but it is a large cut to both inheritance and gift taxes. She opposes new levies on large inheritances.

positions.summary: Le Pen commits to bringing the legal retirement age back from 64 to 62, and to 60 for long careers. The estimated cost is about EUR 9bn per year.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: commits to returning from age 64 to 'age 62, or even 60 for certain salaried workers'; cost about EUR 9bn a year.
Retraite possible dès 60 ans pour les carrières longues
Marine Le Pen promet que le RN gardera la retraite a 62 ans dans son programme

positions.nuance: The X post could not be opened (HTTP 402), so it is unverified. Two neutral aggregators corroborate the position. Financing caveats and any timing flexibility were not checked.

positions.summary: Firmly opposes raising the age; wants to lower it.

sources.quote: Opposition ferme à toute réforme repoussant l'âge légal

positions.nuance: Consistent with ret1.

positions.summary: Le Pen supports voluntary funded (capitalisation) supplementary pensions on top of pay-as-you-go, and says they should remain voluntary. That means she does not support a mandatory component.

sources.quote: Paraphrase of Le Pen: offer French people the means to build complementary retirement through capitalisation, kept voluntary.

positions.nuance: MonVote codes her 'plutôt pour' capitalisation in general. On the MANDATORY component in the statement she is against, but she is open to voluntary funding, hence -1.

positions.summary: Pledges a deficit below 3% by 2030, with savings mainly from immigration, the EU contribution and fraud. Bardella floated EUR 100bn of savings in exchange for an ECB debt deal, but the RN rejects 'austerity'.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: Bardella committed to returning below 3% by 2030 and proposed EUR 100bn of savings tied to ECB debt buybacks.

positions.nuance: Mixed: the 3% target is a priority, but the programme also promises tax cuts and spending increases and does not embrace 'large spending cuts' as such.

positions.summary: No general cut in civil-servant numbers. She proposes abolishing the ARS (regional health agencies) and cutting hospital administrative posts to 10% to free resources for care staff, which is a redeployment.

sources.quote: supprimer les ARS et réduire à 10% les postes administratifs dans les hôpitaux pour libérer des moyens pour les soignants

positions.nuance: The proposal concerns hospital admin posts, redirected to frontline staff, and does not cut the overall number of civil servants. The RN also promises more police, judges and carers. Single aggregator source.

positions.summary: Has no objective of launching large debt-financed public investment programmes and criticises green-transition spending. She defends public services through savings elsewhere.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: no objective to launch major public investment programmes; MonVote codes her 'tout à fait contre' on its deficit/investment question.

positions.nuance: MonVote's exact question wording is unknown, so this is kept at -1 with low confidence.

positions.summary: No evidence found on a constitutional golden rule.
positions.nuance: Not found. Absent from the MonVote2027 and Candidats-presidentielle-2027 pages, and further web search was unavailable during verification.

positions.summary: Against large SMIC increases: the RN voted against a 2022 amendment raising the SMIC to EUR 1,500 net. She prefers employer-contribution exemptions to fund wage rises of up to 10%.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: voted against the 2022 amendment raising SMIC to EUR 1,500 net; says SMIC rises create unemployment risk.

positions.nuance: Coded -1 because she supports wage rises through other channels. Aggregator only.

positions.summary: The RN opposed the 2019 and 2023 unemployment-insurance tightening. It supports activity conditions for the RSA but no clear cut to unemployment insurance.
positions.nuance: Recalled from past votes and not verified. MonVote2027 does not cover unemployment insurance, and search was unavailable.

positions.summary: Supports counterparts for social benefits, and the RN supports keeping the RSA conditional on activity hours. The RSA is to be reserved to French nationals under national priority.

sources.quote: Je pense qu'il faut des contreparties aux aides sociales de ce type qui sont versees. (Bardella, 2024)

positions.nuance: The quote is from Bardella as party president, which counts as the party position. Nothing personal from Le Pen was found.

positions.summary: Opposes cutting working time. She wants firms to be able to move away from 35 hours through branch agreements, which means flexibility upward, not toward 32 hours.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: companies should be able to 'return on 35 hours through branch agreements'.

positions.nuance: Aggregator only.

positions.summary: Wants a sharp reduction of legal immigration with binding annual quotas, an end to family reunification, and asylum applications made from abroad.

sources.quote: Il faut réduire fortement l'immigration légale, en fixant des quotas annuels contraignants.
Paraphrase: family reunification could be hardened or limited by law; asylum applications filed outside France.

positions.nuance: Student and work migration specifics are not detailed.

positions.summary: Calls for a referendum on immigration and citizenship: she demanded one on droit du sol in 2025, and plans a constitutional referendum 'Citoyenneté-Identité-Immigration' as a first act in 2027.

sources.quote: Il y a une chose qui est mieux que le débat, c'est le vote
Paraphrase: Article 11 referendum on a 'Citoyenneté-Identité-Immigration' bill, first deposited January 2024.

positions.nuance: The Article 11 route is legally disputed; her position is firm.

positions.summary: Wants the AME abolished in its current form. The RN's long-standing proposal replaces it with urgent-care-only aid.

sources.quote: Suppression du regroupement familial et de l'AME dans sa forme actuelle

positions.nuance: The urgent-care replacement comes from the 2022 programme and RN line; the 2026 source confirms only the suppression 'in its current form'.

positions.summary: Clearly opposes regularising undocumented workers in shortage occupations.

sources.quote: Opposition nette

positions.nuance: Consistent with the RN's opposition to the regularisation article of the 2023 immigration law (recalled, not re-verified).

positions.summary: National priority for housing, jobs and benefits is central, to be enshrined in the constitution.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: establish 'national priority' in employment, housing and social benefits.
Les prestations sociales non contributives doivent être réservées aux Français (priorité nationale).

positions.nuance: None.

positions.summary: Wants to abolish automatic acquisition of nationality by birth in France, by referendum.

sources.quote: Est-ce que vous êtes d'accord pour le projet de loi supprimant l'acquisition de la nationalité par le droit du sol ?
supprimer le droit du sol et de limiter l'accès à la nationalité à la naturalisation

positions.nuance: None.

positions.summary: The RN consistently opposes local voting rights for non-EU foreigners; no contrary evidence was found.
positions.nuance: Recalled party line that could not be retrieved; France-Vote's immigration page does not cover it. Confidence lowered because no source was found.

positions.summary: Backs mandatory minimum sentences for recidivists and violent crimes, and the end of automatic sentence reductions.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: implementation of minimum sentences, elimination of automatic sentence reductions.

positions.nuance: Aggregator only.

positions.summary: Wants to end the 'excuse of minority' and lower the age of criminal majority to 16.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: end the excuse of minority and lower criminal majority to 16 for repeat offenders.

positions.nuance: Aggregator only. The RN framing targets repeat offenders, which is broader than the statement's 'serious crimes'.

positions.summary: Against an independent police oversight or investigation authority. Bodycams are proposed to protect officers, not as civilian oversight.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: against an independent investigation authority; mandatory body cameras for police self-protection.

positions.nuance: Bodycams are not independent oversight, so -1 understated the opposition. Single aggregator source, hence low confidence.

positions.summary: Opposes cannabis legalisation and backs zero tolerance.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: legalisation sends 'a dramatic signal' and would be 'a catastrophe for our youth'.

positions.nuance: Aggregator only.

positions.summary: The RN voted for algorithmic video surveillance for the 2024 Olympics, and Bardella (2026) backs developing facial recognition in public spaces. That goes beyond the statement.

sources.quote: Nous sommes favorables à ce qu'on développe la reconnaissance faciale pour favoriser l'identification des perturbateurs et des prédateurs. (Bardella, 2026)

positions.nuance: The quote is from Bardella as party president. Backing facial recognition is stronger than the AI video-surveillance rollout in the statement.

positions.summary: Wants constitutional primacy of national law over European law.

sources.quote: Inscrire dans la Constitution la primauté du droit national sur le droit européen

positions.nuance: None.

positions.summary: The RN opposes EU federal debt mutualisation; no direct 2026 source was retrieved.
positions.nuance: Recalled party line. Not found on the aggregators checked, and search was unavailable.

positions.summary: The programme calls for renegotiating France's contribution to the EU budget, with the aim of reducing it.

sources.quote: Renégociation de la contribution française au budget de l'UE

positions.nuance: A reduction is implied but not quantified here; savings on the EU contribution also feature in fin1.

positions.summary: Defends a Europe of sovereign nations and opposes any further transfer of sovereignty. That implies keeping the national veto in foreign policy.

sources.quote: Transformant l'UE en alliance d'États-nations souverains
tout transfert supplémentaire de souveraineté

positions.nuance: No explicit statement on unanimity in foreign policy; deduced from her stated opposition to any further transfer of sovereignty.

positions.summary: Wants to put the Constitution above EU rules and limit the effect of international and EU law, which would allow non-application where they block her programme.

sources.quote: Paraphrase: the text aims to strengthen constitutional supremacy by limiting how international and EU law applies domestically.

positions.nuance: Paraphrase; consistent with eu1.

positions.summary: Rejects Frexit and euro exit; advocates treaty renegotiation.

sources.quote: Renégociation de certains traités, primauté du droit national sur le droit européen sur certaines questions
Paraphrase: RN officially abandoned Frexit; Bardella denied a 'hidden Frexit'; codes her 'plutôt contre'.

positions.nuance: She reversed her 2017 euro-exit position. MonVote codes her 'plutôt contre' rather than 'tout à fait contre', but the RN explicitly rejects leaving the EU.
