result.bio: Raphaël Glucksmann (born 15 October 1979) is a French essayist, documentary filmmaker and politician, son of philosopher André Glucksmann. He co-founded Place publique in 2018 and has been a Member of the European Parliament (S&D group) since 2 July 2019, leading the PS-Place publique list in 2019 (6.2%) and 2024 (13.83%, third place). He has co-led Place publique with Aurore Lalucq since December 2022. On 23 August 2026, on TF1's evening news, he announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election through the joint PS-Place publique primary held in October 2026.

offices.office: Member of the European Parliament (France; S&D group)
Chair of the European Parliament Special Committee on Foreign Interference in all Democratic Processes (INGE)
Co-president of Place publique (with Aurore Lalucq)
Special adviser to Georgian President Mikheil Saakashvili

delivery.what: Human-rights work on China in the European Parliament (Xinjiang, forced labour in supply chains), which led China to sanction him in 2021 (Wikipedia reports the sanctions were lifted in April 2025, when China lifted sanctions on sitting MEPs); led a seven-MEP delegation to Taiwan in November 2021.
delivery.assessment: Documented on Wikipedia; the April 2025 lifting of sanctions on MEPs is confirmed by press reports, but none of the snippets seen names Glucksmann individually. No multi-lean assessment of impact could be gathered.

delivery.what: Chaired the European Parliament special committee on foreign interference (elected chair 23 September 2020); proposed a EUR 100bn European defence fund in the 2024 campaign.
delivery.assessment: Chairmanship confirmed by French and English Wikipedia; legislative outcomes and a balanced assessment were not verified. The EUR 100bn proposal is taken from the original draft and was not re-verified.

media_portrayal.left_media: Not researched: outlet-level coverage could not be gathered (web search budget exhausted).
media_portrayal.right_media: Not researched: outlet-level coverage could not be gathered (web search budget exhausted).
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Not systematically researched. Recent coverage across outlets (Politico, Le Monde, Mediapart, Le Parisien, Ouest-France, Sud Ouest, CNews) reported two episodes: a campaign memo on 'target audiences' leaked by Politico on 12 May 2026, which he called stolen and of no political value, and a video recorded on 17 September 2026 and released by Le Média on 2 October, in which he insulted Mélenchon and Le Pen and said Ségolène Royal had done 'la danse du ventre' for Macron; he apologised to Royal for 'inelegant' remarks during the 4 October primary debate.

result.sources_note: Sources consulted: the French and English Wikipedia articles on Glucksmann (via WebFetch summaries), plus Bing News result listings used to confirm the dates of his candidacy announcement (TF1, 23 August 2026; reported by BFMTV, TF1 Info, Valeurs actuelles, Le Temps), the May 2026 memo leak (20 Minuten, citing Politico), and the October 2026 video and apology (Le Parisien, Ouest-France, Sud Ouest, CNews). The WebSearch budget was exhausted, and no primary sources (programme, roll-call votes) were verified. The legal list is empty because Wikipedia does not mention any personal judicial case, complaint or investigation, but no dedicated court or press check was possible. Reversals and traits stay empty because the two-source, different-lean rule could not be met. Possible reversal candidates that were not documented to the required standard: his stance on LFI (he ran with the Nouveau Front populaire in 2024, then called for the left to distance itself from LFI). Wikipedia notes policy positions: very cautious use of the word 'genocide' about Gaza while denouncing a 'massacre' and the blockade, rejection of an alliance with LFI, leaving Dublin III, criticism of the 2024 EU Migration and Asylum Pact, support for wealth taxation, and support for Ukraine's EU integration. A rerun with a higher search budget is recommended.

positions.summary: Opposes any tax increase, including on the highest earners and wealth; no sign of support for an ISF return.

sources.quote: Une opposition à la taxe Zucman... et à toute hausse des impôts.
s'oppose à toute hausse d'impôt pour les plus riches

positions.nuance: There is no explicit 2026 quote on the ISF itself. The coding rests on his general refusal to raise taxes on the wealthy (2020 and 2025).

positions.summary: Explicitly rejected the Zucman tax, saying investors would leave France.

sources.quote: si demain on appliquait la taxe Zucman, les investisseurs quitteraient la France

positions.summary: Programme: cut social contributions by 30 bn euros and abolish most production taxes (CVAE, C3S, CFE) for 40 bn euros.

sources.quote: 30 milliards d'euros de cotisations en moins ... suppressions drastiques ... d'une majorité des impôts de production

positions.summary: Fiercely opposed the EU-Mercosur free-trade deal to protect French agriculture, and threatened censure if Macron voted for it.

sources.quote: Mercosur : Emmanuel Macron « prend le risque d'une censure » du gouvernement s'il vote pour l'accord de libre-échange, prévient Bruno Retailleau (headline)

positions.nuance: This is a partial match. Opposing a trade deal is not an explicit call for new tariffs or quotas, and his wider programme is pro-business and liberal.

positions.summary: No current evidence that he supports renationalising energy or motorways.
positions.nuance: In 2005 he opposed motorway privatisation (Wikipedia fr). Opposing a sale does not mean backing renationalisation, and nothing recent was found. In 2026 his energy focus is nuclear investment.

positions.summary: Pledged to be the president who lowers inheritance taxes.

sources.quote: Je ne serai pas le président qui augmentera les droits de succession mais celui qui les baissera

positions.nuance: He made the pledge in L'Opinion on 26-27 August 2026.

positions.summary: Pension plan: minimum age 63 with a 7%/year penalty, and the full rate at 65. He does not return to 62.

sources.quote: L'âge minimal de départ, c'est 63 ans

positions.nuance: His minimum age of 63 is below today's 64, but only with a heavy penalty, and the full rate moves to 65. He remains clearly against 62 or lower.

positions.summary: Sets an automatic full-rate age of 65, indexed to life expectancy, while allowing departure from 63 with a penalty.

sources.quote: le départ à taux plein automatique serait fixé à 65 ans
un âge de départ minimal à 63 ans pour une carrière complète

positions.nuance: This is a partial match: the effective 'âge d'équilibre' rises to 65, while the minimum legal age falls to 63.

positions.summary: Proposes a capitalisation component for young workers: 1% of gross salary, split employee/employer, aiming for 25-30% of their future pensions.

sources.quote: 25 à 30% des retraites des jeunes
une part de retraite par capitalisation 'pour les jeunes'

positions.nuance: No source we could open says whether it is mandatory. The employer-plus-employee contribution design suggests a generalised scheme, but that is unverified, so +1 rather than +2.

positions.summary: Warns of a 'Greek scenario' and backs an emergency spending-cut plan: capping welfare at 70% of SMIC, fewer civil servants and a pension reform.

sources.quote: Un jour, on va avoir un pépin

positions.nuance: His priority on spending cuts is clear. No explicit 3%-deficit date was verified.

positions.summary: Wants to cut public-sector headcount, citing a figure of 600,000 fewer public agents over ten years, and to stop replacing retirees systematically.

sources.quote: engager une réduction des effectifs dans la fonction publique, en cessant de remplacer systématiquement les départs à la retraite
Bruno Retailleau vise 600 000 agents publics en moins sur dix ans (related headline)

positions.summary: Treats debt as an imminent danger and wants to reduce borrowing, not increase it.

sources.quote: On lève plus de 30 milliards d'euros d'emprunts par mois pour faire face à la dette.

positions.nuance: His backing for a golden-rule referendum (see fin4) supports this coding.

positions.summary: Calls for a referendum before end-2026 to write a budget golden rule into the Constitution.

sources.quote: le seul bouclier, c'est le référendum, une règle d'or

positions.summary: Called a sharp SMIC increase 'désolante' (2018). He now raises take-home pay through contribution cuts, not the SMIC.

sources.quote: Il qualifie également de « désolante » la forte hausse du SMIC préconisée par ... Guillaume Peltier
Des rabais de cotisations défendus par Bruno Retailleau ... jusqu'au Smic porté à 1 700 euros voulu par Jean-Luc Mélenchon

positions.nuance: The explicit SMIC quote dates from 2018. In 2026 his purchasing-power route is cutting contributions and paying for extra hours, not raising the SMIC.

positions.summary: Wants to be 'less generous' on unemployment insurance and to revive the Attal unemployment-benefit reform.

sources.quote: être moins généreux sur l'assurance chômage
relancer la réforme de l'assurance chômage, en reprenant la réforme Attal

positions.summary: Proposes a 'revenu d'incitation à l'activité' that makes 15 hours of activity mandatory for RSA recipients.

sources.quote: en rendant obligatoire les 15 heures d'activité complémentaire au RSA

positions.summary: Wants to remove the 35 hours from the Labour Code and raise working time, the opposite of 32 hours.

sources.quote: Les 35 heures seraient ainsi supprimées du Code du travail

positions.nuance: His 2019 position was a return to 39 hours. In 2026 he favours abolishing the statutory 35 hours, with extra hours exempt from contributions.

positions.summary: Wants to reduce legal immigration: curbs on student visas (fees, resources, quotas by field), changes to family reunification via the EU directive, and tighter asylum.

sources.quote: Si nous voulons stopper l'immigration illégale et réduire l'immigration légale, il faudra le faire avec fermeté et méthode.
une loi pour réduire l'immigration

positions.summary: Pledges a constitutional revision to widen the referendum, then a referendum on an immigration law early in his term.

sources.quote: Je prends cet engagement que ce seront les Français qui enfin définiront la politique migratoire
soumettre aux Français, dans les premiers mois de mon mandat, un projet de loi complet sur l'immigration

positions.summary: Proposes abolishing the AME and replacing it with a narrower scheme. He has long advocated switching to an urgent-care aid (AMU).

sources.quote: Il propose également de supprimer l'aide médicale d'État (AME)
AME trop chère, B. Retailleau réaffirme sa volonté de passer à l'AMU (headline)

positions.nuance: The 2026 article paraphrases the replacement scheme oddly ('contre-aide'). The urgent-care (AMU) form is attested from 2024.

positions.summary: As minister he repealed the Valls circular (seven years' presence required, regularisation 'exceptional'). As candidate he rejects regularising workers for labour-shortage sectors.

sources.quote: l'idée de régulariser des clandestins qui ont fraudé nos lois est une capitulation
Elle abroge la « circulaire Valls » et durcit les critères que celle-ci imposait.

positions.nuance: His 2025 circular told prefects to favour the statutory labour-shortage route among the few exceptional regularisations. His overall stance is clearly against, and in 2026 he explicitly rejects the labour-shortage argument.

positions.summary: Wants to make foreigners' access to welfare conditional on five years of legal residence and work. This is a residence condition, not an explicit national-priority rule.

sources.quote: Je veux conditionner l'accès aux aides sociales, pour les étrangers, à cinq ans de résidence légale et de travail.

positions.nuance: This is a partial version. No quote was found backing priority for French citizens in social housing.

positions.summary: Wants to abolish droit du sol nationwide, by referendum.

sources.quote: On ne peut pas devenir français par hasard, en catimini, de façon automatique.
Bruno Retailleau souhaite supprimer le droit du sol par référendum (headline)

positions.summary: LR opposes local voting rights for non-EU foreigners. No personal 2025-2026 quote from Retailleau was verified.
positions.nuance: This is the party line plus consistency with his citizenship-restriction agenda. It was not verified live.

positions.summary: Wants mandatory minimum sentences ('peines minimales') so the judge 'has no choice', citing attacks on police, gendarmes and firefighters.

sources.quote: je veux des peines minimales pour que quand on tabasse un policier, un gendarme, un pompier, le juge n'ait pas le choix

positions.nuance: His example targets attacks on emergency workers. A recidivist-specific scope was not verified.

positions.summary: Wants to lower the age of criminal majority to 15, going beyond the statement.

sources.quote: Pour les mineurs, je veux abaisser la majorité pénale à 15 ans.

positions.nuance: His position hardened from 16 (2025 'révolution pénale') to 15 in September 2026.

positions.summary: As Interior Minister he consistently defended the police. No statement on an independent oversight body was found.
positions.nuance: This is inferred from his record.

positions.summary: Declared himself 'totally against' legalising cannabis and said legalisation 'doesn't work'.

sources.quote: La légalisation du cannabis, « ça ne marche pas », estime Bruno Retailleau (headline)
Bruno Retailleau se dit « totalement contre » (headline)

positions.summary: As minister he pushed for systematic CCTV ('vidéoprotection'), and the government he sat in sought to extend algorithmic video surveillance.

sources.quote: a de nouveau évoqué une mise en place systématique de la « vidéoprotection »

positions.nuance: His backing for generalising AI-assisted surveillance specifically is not confirmed by a quote of his own, and the source is a critical left-wing outlet.

positions.summary: Proposes a 'constitutional shield' letting French law prevail over EU law in certain situations (immigration, security).

sources.quote: permettre, dans certaines situations, au droit français de primer sur le droit européen

positions.nuance: This is partial: it applies in certain cases (fundamental interests) and not as a general rule of French-law primacy. He voted against Maastricht and Lisbon.

positions.summary: No evidence found on EU joint borrowing.
positions.nuance: A brief search found nothing personal.

positions.summary: No evidence found on France's EU budget contribution.
positions.nuance: A brief search found nothing personal.

positions.summary: No evidence found on unanimity in EU foreign policy.
positions.nuance: A brief search found nothing.

positions.summary: Wants an organic law able to set aside the effect of European rules and case law contrary to France's 'fundamental interests', so that his immigration and security programme can be implemented.

sources.quote: permettre à une loi organique, dans certains cas, d'écarter l'effet d'une jurisprudence européenne contraire aux « intérêts fondamentaux » de la France
un « bouclier constitutionnel » afin de permettre, dans certaines situations, au droit français de primer sur le droit européen

positions.nuance: The statement's 'some EU rules' wording matches his 'in certain cases' mechanism. He also says he will change EU rules from within (e.g. the family reunification directive).

positions.summary: Does not call for leaving the EU. He wants to change EU rules from inside and sees a right-leaning Europe as a source of French influence.

sources.quote: Dans une Europe qui se droitise, ce sera la condition de notre influence.

positions.nuance: The 'no exit' reading comes from his reform-from-within stance; no explicit anti-Frexit quote was found.

positions.summary: Place publique's 2025 programme, co-signed by Glucksmann, calls for a drastic increase in military aid to Ukraine. That fits his 2024 call for a war-economy posture.

sources.quote: Augmenter drastiquement l'aide militaire à l'Ukraine qui est notre première ligne de défense
paraphrase: France should fully enter a war economy to help Ukraine (2024 European campaign)

positions.nuance: The programme is dated June 2025 and Glucksmann is co-director of the publication. I found no sign that he changed this position before October 2026.

positions.summary: No verified evidence on sending French troops to guarantee a ceasefire.
positions.nuance: The 2025 programme covers aid, a European defence fund and extending nuclear deterrence, but says nothing about a reassurance force. Web search was exhausted, so I could not check 2025-2026 interviews. Do not infer a position.

positions.summary: In 2019 he said France must stay in NATO. Nothing found on the integrated military command specifically.

sources.quote: paraphrase: France must remain in NATO and maintain NATO-EU relations (Marianne, 2019)

positions.nuance: Staying in NATO is a different question from staying in its integrated command. The 2025 programme does not mention NATO and stresses European defence instead. The only source is an old statement relayed second-hand.

positions.summary: Place publique (August 2026) calls for suspending the EU-Israel association agreement.

sources.quote: Conditionner la coopération avec Israël au respect du droit international et suspendre l'accord d'association UE-Israël.

positions.nuance: This is a party communiqué from Glucksmann's party, which he co-chairs, not a verified personal statement. It justifies suspension mainly by West Bank colonisation and international law, not only by the conduct of the Gaza war. He has also refused to call Gaza a 'genocide' (2024).

positions.summary: No national target as a share of GDP found. The programme proposes a 500 bn EUR European defence fund financed by joint borrowing.

sources.quote: fonds européen de défense de 500 milliards d'euros via un emprunt commun

positions.nuance: His hawkish line on defence makes support likely, but there is no evidence on the wording '>3% of GDP', so it is not coded.

positions.summary: The programme wants to recreate a universal republican rite of passage at majority to replace military service. It does not say it would be compulsory or military.

sources.quote: Travailler à recréer un rite de passage républicain et universel autour de la majorité pour remplacer le service militaire

positions.nuance: 'Universal' points towards something for everyone, close to a national service. Whether it would be compulsory, and what it would contain, is not specified, so this is a weaker version of the statement.

positions.summary: Wants an immediate ban on Russian gas imports. Nothing found specifically on lifting sanctions in exchange for a peace deal.

sources.quote: Interdire immédiatement toute importation de gaz russe
paraphrase: advocates ending imports of Russian gas and oil (Le Monde tribune)

positions.nuance: Inferred from a consistently hawkish stance on Russia, hence low confidence.

positions.summary: No evidence found on low-emission zones (ZFE).
positions.nuance: The 2025 programme does not mention ZFE. Web search was exhausted.

positions.summary: The programme wants to ban the most harmful pesticides, including glyphosate and neonicotinoids, and to impose mirror clauses on imports.

sources.quote: interdisant les pesticides les plus néfastes, glyphosate, néonicotinoïdes tueurs d'abeilles

positions.nuance: The EU has authorised glyphosate until 2033, so a French ban means banning what competitors use. The programme pairs the ban with 'mesures miroirs' to shield farmers from imports that do not meet the same standards, and does not use the 'even if competitors' framing explicitly.

positions.summary: No explicit evidence on the 2035 end of combustion-car sales.
positions.nuance: The programme backs small affordable electric cars, social leasing and 100%-electric fleets for large companies. That suggests support, but the 2035 deadline is not mentioned and his position on the 2025-26 EU revision is unverified.

positions.summary: Wants to end the VAT and kerosene-tax exemptions, extend the ban on domestic flights and tax private jets.

sources.quote: suppression des exonérations de TVA et de taxe sur le kérosène, étendre l'interdiction des vols intérieurs ... taxation des plus gros pollueurs individuels (jets privés

positions.nuance: Covers all three items in the statement.

positions.summary: No evidence on ranking climate above economic growth.
positions.nuance: The programme frames ecology as compatible with 'puissance' and industrial growth and never states a trade-off.

positions.summary: Wants to strengthen nuclear's role, including building new units on time. It does not commit beyond the six planned EPR2.

sources.quote: Conforter le rôle du nucléaire, énergie pilotable et décarbonée, en assurant ... la construction à temps de nouvelles unités.

positions.nuance: Supports a weaker version: new reactors yes, but how many is unspecified, and 'à temps' points to the programme already planned.

positions.summary: Opposes phasing out nuclear: the programme wants to strengthen nuclear's role, and in 2024 he said exiting cannot be an objective.

sources.quote: Conforter le rôle du nucléaire, énergie pilotable et décarbonée
paraphrase: exiting nuclear 'cannot be an objective'

positions.nuance: In 2024 he avoided a firm line. By 2025 the programme clearly supports nuclear.

positions.summary: Wants a large multi-year investment plan in all renewables, wind included.

sources.quote: Lancer un grand plan d'investissement pluriannuel dans toutes les énergies renouvelables ... soleil, vent

positions.nuance: Halting wind development is not addressed directly, but it contradicts the stated plan.

positions.summary: Wants part of electricity bills based on French production costs instead of the volatile market price. Leaving the European market is not proposed.

sources.quote: Fixer une partie de la facture ... sur le coût de production de notre électricité nucléaire et renouvelable, et non plus sur un prix de marché

positions.nuance: He shares the goal of cost-based prices but proposes doing it within the EU framework; his pro-European federalist line makes exiting the market unlikely. Inferred, hence low confidence.

positions.summary: Wants a more parliamentary regime (PM invested by the Assembly, constructive censure) and a citizens' convention laying the basis of a constituent assembly to change the Constitution.

sources.quote: une grande convention citoyenne qui jettera les bases d'une assemblée constituante pour changer la Constitution.

positions.nuance: The programme does not use the label 'VIe République', but the substance (a new constitution, a parliamentary shift) matches the statement.

positions.summary: Wants proportional representation introduced immediately, preferably with regional constituencies.

sources.quote: Instaurer immédiatement la proportionnelle, de préférence par circonscriptions régionales

positions.summary: Wants a citizens' initiative right that can trigger local and national referendums.

sources.quote: Instaurer un droit d'initiative citoyenne, permettant de déclencher des séquences démocratiques avec des référendums à l'échelle locale et nationale

positions.nuance: The programme does not call it a 'RIC' and leaves the design vague ('séquences démocratiques'), so this is coded as a partial version.

positions.summary: Wants a constructive vote of no confidence that would end Article 49.3.

sources.quote: censure “constructive” ... ce qui permettra de mettre fin au 49.3.

positions.summary: No evidence on widening referendums to immigration or justice.
positions.nuance: Not addressed in the 2025 programme. Web search was exhausted.

positions.summary: No evidence found on assisted dying.
positions.nuance: Not in the 2025 programme. His EP role means no French vote record. Web search was exhausted.

positions.summary: No evidence found.
positions.nuance: Not addressed in the programme. Web search was exhausted.

positions.nuance: Not addressed in the programme. Web search was exhausted.

positions.summary: The programme 'firmly defends' laïcité as liberty of conscience plus an emancipation principle. It neither proposes nor rejects new restrictions on citizens.

sources.quote: Elle garantit la liberté de conscience et de culte, mais ne se limite pas à la tolérance : elle est un principe d'émancipation.

positions.nuance: Too ambiguous to code on the statement's 'without further restricting' clause.

positions.summary: No evidence found on surrogacy (GPA).
positions.nuance: Not addressed in the programme. Web search was exhausted.

positions.summary: No evidence found on school uniforms.
positions.nuance: Not addressed in the programme.

positions.summary: Wants fewer pupils per teacher in primary school and a trial in secondary, plus a pay rise for all teachers over 5 years.

sources.quote: Réduire le nombre d'élèves par enseignant en primaire et l'expérimenter dans le second degré

positions.nuance: A weaker version: there is no 'massive' hiring commitment, and secondary school would only get a trial.

positions.summary: No evidence found on ability grouping.
positions.nuance: Not addressed in the programme.

positions.summary: Wants state-contracted private schools brought into the school catchment map (carte scolaire) to improve social mix. Cutting their funding is not mentioned.

sources.quote: Intégrer les établissements privés sous contrat à la carte scolaire pour garantir une répartition équitable des élèves et renforcer la mixité sociale.

positions.nuance: Shares the goal (social mix) through a different tool; no funding sanction is proposed.

positions.summary: Wants to 'deeply rethink' Parcoursup through consultation. Abolishing it or ending selection is not proposed.

sources.quote: Repenser en profondeur Parcoursup à travers une concertation réunissant parents, étudiants, universités

positions.nuance: The programme wants to reform Parcoursup, not abolish it, which counts as partial opposition to the statement.

positions.summary: The programme only says it wants to 'support' doctors setting up in practice. It mentions no obligation and does not reject one.

sources.quote: Soutenir l'installation, diversifier les pratiques et valoriser les évolutions de carrières

positions.nuance: The wording suggests incentives, but it is not explicit enough to code.

positions.summary: Place publique strongly opposes the July 2026 government plan to double medical franchises, calling it unjust and ineffective.

sources.quote: Place publique s'oppose avec force à ce type de mesures injustes et inefficaces.

positions.nuance: This is a party communiqué, not a verified personal statement by Glucksmann (party co-chair).

positions.summary: Wants rent caps in high-pressure housing areas.

sources.quote: Encadrer les loyers dans les zones en grande tension pour garantir l'accès au logement aux ménages modestes.

positions.nuance: 'Zones en grande tension' corresponds closely to the statement's 'areas with housing shortages'.

positions.summary: Wants to reverse 'the dogma of free and undistorted competition' and end competition between public administrations and the private sector.

sources.quote: Revenir sur le dogme de la concurrence libre et non faussée

positions.nuance: Clear opposition to more competition in general, but nothing specific on liberalising transport or energy, hence -1.

positions.summary: No ISF-style wealth tax in Attal's programme. He promises to cut the deficit without raising taxes and opposes higher taxes on savings, life insurance and inheritance.

sources.quote: une stratégie de réduction du déficit sans hausse d'impôts
Ce n'est pas avec l'épargne des Français qu'on va rembourser la dette française.

positions.nuance: No explicit statement on reinstating the ISF was retrieved. The code is inferred from his no-tax-rise platform and his opposition to the Zucman tax (see eco2).

positions.summary: The Assemblée rejected the Zucman tax (2% on fortunes over EUR 100m) on 31 Oct 2025 by 228 to 172. The bloc central, which includes the Renaissance group Attal chairs, opposed it and called it a 'mirage'.

sources.quote: était considérée comme un " mirage " par le bloc central
rejetée par l'Assemblée nationale, avec 228 voix contre et 172 pour

positions.nuance: Group-level vote. Attal's personal roll-call vote was not checked on datan/assemblee-nationale. He commented after the rejection (BFM, 31 Oct 2025) that a compromise 'ne plaît pas à tout le monde'. A 2026 Le Figaro piece on candidates' tax plans (paywalled) was not read.

positions.summary: Attal's 'droit au brut' lowers social contributions (the programme names employee charges, 'charges salariales') to raise net pay. He also says labour costs should not have risen since 2024. No pledge to cut production taxes or employer contributions specifically was found.

sources.quote: en réduisant les charges salariales pour faire monter le salaire net
il aurait fallu "ne pas augmenter le coût du travail depuis 2024"

positions.nuance: Partial support. The statement names production taxes and employer contributions. His flagship cut targets employee contributions; he opposes raising employer costs but does not clearly pledge to lower them.

positions.summary: No evidence found on national tariffs or quotas to protect French sectors.
positions.nuance: A brief search found nothing. His economic federalism ('disparition totale des frontières économiques' within an EU core) points away from national tariffs, but that is not coded.

positions.summary: No evidence found on bringing energy or motorways back under public control.
positions.nuance: A brief search found nothing. The dette-écologique programme page discusses energy independence but does not mention EDF or nationalisation.

positions.summary: Opposes any rise in inheritance taxation and wants to make lifetime gifts easier and smoother (to grandchildren, great-nephews and great-nieces).

sources.quote: faciliter et fluidifier les donations du vivant

positions.nuance: Partial support. No explicit cut to inheritance tax rates; he blocks increases and eases gift transfers.

positions.summary: Wants to abolish the legal retirement age and move to a universal system based on contribution duration, with a real penalty for leaving early and a real bonus for leaving late. He rejects parametric fixes, so he does not support returning to 62.

sources.quote: une vraie décote si vous partez tôt, une vraie surcote si vous partez tard
il redit vouloir supprimer l'âge légal de départ pour mettre en place un système universel avec une part de capitalisation

positions.nuance: His current position (abolish the legal age) replaces the earlier defence of the 2023 reform at 64. The 2023 reform has since been suspended at 62 years and 9 months. Without a legal age, early departure would still be possible, but with a strong penalty.

positions.summary: Rejects raising the legal age (he called Philippe's 65 plan 'palliative care' and said 'On n'en est plus à bouger les paramètres'). He prefers abolishing the legal age, with a penalty/bonus system based on contribution duration.

sources.quote: On n'en est plus à bouger les paramètres ou les curseurs

positions.nuance: Coded -1, not -2: he opposes a higher legal age, but his system aims to make people work longer through strong penalties and bonuses.

positions.summary: Proposes a universal system 'avec une part de capitalisation' ('a real capitalisation pillar'), a state-funded EUR 1,000 retirement savings plan per child, and 50% of profit-sharing directed to retirement savings plans.

sources.quote: un système universel avec une part de capitalisation
l'ouverture d'un plan d'épargne retraite de 1000€ par l'État

positions.nuance: Sources do not say whether the capitalisation part would be mandatory. If it is built into the universal system it could be compulsory, which would make it +2. Kept at +1 until the mechanism is confirmed.

positions.summary: Zero deficit in at most 10 years (balanced budget by 2037), up to EUR 150bn in savings, no tax rises, and a voluntary-departure plan for 100,000 civil servants. As PM in 2024 he cut ministry budgets by EUR 10bn.

sources.quote: L'objectif est clair : zéro déficit en 10 ans maximum.
un objectif de retour à l'équilibre des finances publiques en 2037

positions.nuance: His target (zero deficit) is stricter than the 3% threshold. He frames it as 'rigoureuse et sérieuse' rather than austerity.

positions.summary: Pledges to cut 100,000 civil-service posts through a voluntary-departure plan with a severance bonus, and to remove one layer of local government.

sources.quote: un plan de départs volontaires de 100.000 fonctionnaires, accompagné d'une prime de départ
L'objectif affiché est de supprimer 100.000 postes

positions.nuance: Reached through attrition and voluntary departures. Education, the armed forces, justice and the interior are reportedly spared.

positions.summary: Treats national debt as a loss of sovereignty and targets zero deficit. He backs EU-level common debt for climate adaptation.

sources.quote: Un pays surendetté est un pays qui abandonne sa souveraineté
dette commune pour financer l'adaptation au dérèglement climatique

positions.nuance: Opposes more national debt but is open to joint EU borrowing for climate, so partial opposition (-1).

positions.summary: No constitutional golden rule found. His fiscal plan includes 'impunité budgétaire zéro' with sanctions, which is not a constitutional deficit cap.
positions.nuance: A brief search (Le Monde/Le Parisien headlines of 2 July 2026) found no golden-rule pledge.

positions.summary: Raises wages through productivity and lower contributions ('droit au brut': +EUR 250 net for a EUR 2,200 net salary), not through faster SMIC increases.

sources.quote: " Droit au brut ", martèle Gabriel Attal (Renaissance)
en réduisant les charges salariales pour faire monter le salaire net

positions.nuance: No pledge to raise the SMIC above inflation. Not explicitly opposed either, hence -1.

positions.summary: As PM (March 2024) he proposed cutting the maximum benefit duration (to no less than 12 months, from 18) and tightening eligibility. His 2027 programme promises an unemployment insurance reform that 'incite au travail' and saves over EUR 4bn.

sources.quote: a préconisé mercredi un durcissement des conditions d'indemnisation du chômage
une réforme de l'assurance chômage permettant de créer 100 000 emplois et d'économiser plus de 4 milliards d'euros

positions.nuance: The 2027 programme does not specify duration or amount cuts, so confidence is medium. The 2024 tightening was halted after the dissolution.

positions.summary: Wants social spending to encourage work. The RSA activity requirement (2023 law) was passed by the government he served in. No 2026 quote on RSA hours.

sources.quote: l'effort devra d'abord porter sur la dépense sociale

positions.nuance: RSA is not mentioned on the programme pages fetched.

positions.summary: Wants people to work more: remove the 220-hour annual overtime cap. Promotes a four-day week only as a reorganisation of existing hours, 'where possible'.

sources.quote: supprimer le plafond d'heures supplémentaires fixé par le Code du travail

positions.nuance: The four-day week means flexible scheduling, not fewer hours.

positions.summary: 'Accueillir moins pour accueillir mieux': a Canada-style points system, family reunification to fall, work to become the first ground for immigration ahead of family and student immigration, and limiting quotas voted by Parliament every two years.

sources.quote: ce que nous voulons, c'est accueillir moins pour accueillir mieux
Je souhaite que l'immigration de travail devienne le premier motif d'immigration au détriment de l'immigration familiale, de l'immigration étudiante

positions.nuance: He wants an overall reduction, but work immigration is prioritised rather than cut sharply, so partial support (+1).

positions.summary: Proposes an annual multi-question referendum day and limiting immigration quotas set by Parliament. No referendum specifically on immigration policy found.

les compétences régaliennes resteraient à la main des États

result.bio: Olivier Faure (born 18 August 1968 in La Tronche, Isère) is a French Socialist politician who joined the PS in 1984. He was deputy chief of staff to François Hollande at the PS (2000-2007) and has been deputy for Seine-et-Marne's 11th constituency since June 2012. He has been First Secretary of the Parti socialiste since April 2018 and was re-elected in 2021, 2023 and June 2025. He backed the NUPES alliance in 2022 and the Nouveau Front populaire in 2024. In July 2025 he helped agree the principle of a common left candidate for 2027, though PS members later voted for a primary limited to the socialist pole. He announced his presidential bid on 30 August 2026, published the book "La loi du plus juste" on 17 September 2026, and is running in the PS/Place publique primary of October 2026.

result.bio: Marine Tondelier (born 23 August 1986, Bois-Bernard, Pas-de-Calais) has been National Secretary of Les Écologistes (formerly EELV) since December 2022 and was re-elected in April 2025. She trained at Sciences Po Lille and was délégué générale of the air-quality federation Atmo France (2017-2022). She sat as an opposition councillor in Hénin-Beaumont from 2014 to March 2026, when her list came second (18.22%) behind the incumbent RN mayor, and has been a Hauts-de-France regional councillor since 2021. She announced her 2027 presidential candidacy on 22 October 2025 and was designated by her party on 8 December 2025.

legal.case: Defamation prosecution brought by Hénin-Beaumont mayor Steeve Briois and Bruno Bilde (RN) over her 2017 book 'Nouvelles du Front'; she was the defendant. The Paris tribunal correctionnel found some statements defamatory but acquitted (relaxe) her on grounds of good faith. No appeal was found in the sources consulted.
legal.date: Judgment reported by France Bleu on 6 November 2020 (Paris tribunal correctionnel); exact judgment day not confirmed

reversals.before: On 18 November 2024 she called X a 'catalyst of hate' and argued for regulating or closing it. On 12 January 2025 she urged the left to leave the platform.
reversals.after: On 19 January 2025 she said no collective departure had happened and that she would stay on X to defend ecology on 'hostile terrain'.

delivery.what: Led the party as National Secretary and was re-elected in the first round with 72.64% on 19 April 2025. She has never held national or local executive office, so she has no ministerial or executive record.

This comes from one secondary source (Wikipedia) and was not corroborated directly.

result.bio: Fabien Roussel (born 16 April 1969 in Béthune) is a former journalist who became national secretary of the Parti communiste français (PCF) on 25 November 2018. He was deputy for Nord's 20th constituency from June 2017 to June 2024 and the PCF's 2022 presidential candidate (2.28%, 8th place). He has been mayor of Saint-Amand-les-Eaux since 30 January 2025 and was re-elected in March 2026. According to French Wikipedia (citing Le Figaro), he announced his 2027 presidential candidacy on TF1 on 6 September 2026 under the slogan "Vivre".

offices.office: National secretary (secrétaire national) of the PCF

legal.case: Mediapart (2022) alleged that Roussel held a fictitious job as parliamentary assistant to PCF deputy Jean-Jacques Candelier (2009-2014). The Parquet national financier opened a preliminary investigation on 11 March 2022. Roussel denies the allegation and says he worked on following conflicts in the Douaisis; Candelier told L'Humanité that Roussel did work as his assistant. No charge (mise en examen) or closure is reported; status taken from French Wikipedia, not confirmed against a court or AFP source.

reversals.before: Advocated France leaving NATO's integrated command, presented as necessary for national independence.
reversals.after: After Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, he no longer proposes French withdrawal from NATO (he still opposes Ukraine joining NATO and the EU).

delivery.what: Deputy 2017-2024 in opposition (PCF / GDR group). He was rapporteur of a bill to create a French list of tax havens (2017-2018). No law adopted under his name is documented in the sources consulted.
delivery.assessment: Legislative record could not be checked against roll-call sites (datan.fr, nosdeputes.fr) or cross-lean outlets; only a secondary source (Wikipedia) was available.

delivery.what: 2022 presidential programme proposals (not enacted): SMIC raised to 1,500 euros net, legal retirement age back to 60, wealth tax restored and tripled, recruitment of 30,000 police, and an energy mix of nuclear and renewables.
delivery.assessment: These are campaign proposals, not delivered measures; the 2027 programme was not verified.

delivery.what: Mayor of Saint-Amand-les-Eaux since 30 January 2025, succeeding Alain Bocquet; his list won the March 2026 municipal election in the first round with 51.06% and he was re-elected mayor on 22 March 2026.
delivery.assessment: Executive record is short (about 1.7 years); no assessment of his municipal record was found in the sources consulted.

media_portrayal.left_media: Not verified directly. Mediapart published the 2022 fictitious-job allegation; Roussel responded by accusing its founder Edwy Plenel of publishing it to favour Mélenchon's candidacy.
media_portrayal.right_media: Not verified directly. Wikipedia records a March 2025 CNews appearance in which he said anti-white racism exists; how right-leaning outlets frame him could not be checked.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Not verified directly; Le Monde, franceinfo, AFP and Public Sénat coverage could not be fetched.

positions.summary: The June 2024 NFP joint programme, which Tondelier co-founded and led for Les Écologistes, includes bringing back the ISF with a climate component.

sources.quote: Rétablissement de l'impôt de solidarité sur la fortune (ISF), incorporation d'une composante climatique

positions.nuance: This is the 2024 coalition programme. No 2026 Tondelier campaign text or personal quote was found, and web search was exhausted during verification.

positions.summary: The 2% minimum tax on ultra-rich fortunes started as a bill tabled by Écologiste group MPs (Eva Sas, Clémentine Autain). The Assembly adopted it on 20 Feb 2025. Les Écologistes back putting it into practice.

sources.quote: présentée le 7 janvier 2025 par Éva Sas et Clémentine Autain, membres du groupe écologiste et social
Les Écologistes, le Parti socialiste et Place publique défendent la mise en œuvre de la taxe Zucman.

positions.nuance: This is Tondelier's own party group's bill. She is not an MP, so there is no personal vote, and no personal quote was retrieved. The Assembly rejected the Zucman amendment to the 2026 budget on 31 Oct 2025.

positions.summary: The Greens generally oppose untargeted cuts to employer contributions and prefer conditional aid. No Tondelier-specific evidence found.
positions.nuance: Political scientist B. Villalba (2012, cited on the party's Wikipedia page) notes that party members diverge on cutting employer contributions. Coded from that inference, so low confidence.

positions.summary: The NFP programme calls for 'social and ecological protectionism' at EU borders, a ban on imports that do not meet social and environmental standards, and rejection of Mercosur/CETA.

sources.quote: Instauration d'une règle verte européenne et d'un protectionnisme social et écologique aux frontières européennes

positions.nuance: Partial support: the protection is EU-level and tied to standards. It is not France-specific sectoral tariffs or quotas. 2024 programme.

positions.summary: The NFP programme refuses privatisation of hydroelectric dams. Full renationalisation of energy or motorways is not explicit in the programme summary.

sources.quote: Refus de la privatisation des barrages hydroélectriques

positions.nuance: Partial: this is public control of some strategic assets. The motorway item is a moratorium on new motorway projects and does not cover taking concessions back. Not verified for 2026.

positions.summary: The NFP programme calls for reforming inheritance tax and creating a 'maximum inheritance', which is the opposite of lowering it.

sources.quote: Réforme de l'impôt sur l'héritage ... Instauration d'un héritage maximum

positions.nuance: 2024 coalition programme. The direction of the 'reform' is set by the maximum-inheritance cap.

positions.summary: The NFP programme calls for repealing the 2023 reform and returning to retirement at 60. Les Écologistes fought the Borne reform, and Tondelier called the Assembly a 'ZAD démocratique' against it.

sources.quote: Abrogation de la réforme des retraites et retour à la retraite à 60 ans
Marine Tondelier qualifie l'Assemblée nationale de « zone à défendre démocratique »

positions.nuance: The target age is 60, below 62, so it fits the statement. 2024 programme. Her 2026 campaign wording was not verified.

positions.summary: She opposed the 2023 increase to 64, and the NFP programme wants to go back to 60, so she opposes raising the age above 64.

sources.quote: Abrogation de la réforme des retraites et retour à la retraite à 60 ans

positions.nuance: Follows directly from ret1.

positions.summary: The Greens defend the pay-as-you-go system, so mandatory capitalisation is unlikely.
positions.nuance: Inferred. No explicit statement found, and search was exhausted.

verification_notes: Method limit: the session's WebSearch budget (200/200) was exhausted, so no news or roll-call searches were possible. Verification used the raw wikitext of the French Wikipedia pages Nouveau_Front_populaire, Les_Écologistes, Taxe_Zucman, Marine_Tondelier and Justice_des_mineurs_en_France (fetched with curl, with quotes checked verbatim), plus the European Greens 2024 French manifesto PDF. lesecologistes.fr returned 403 and huffingtonpost.fr was blocked. No Tondelier 2026 campaign programme text was retrievable. Her documented first priority is a 'sécurité sociale de l'alimentation'.

Context: Tondelier is not an MP, so she has no personal votes. She declared her candidacy on 22 Oct 2025 and was designated by Les Écologistes on 8 Dec 2025. The left primary failed in July 2026. The NFP June 2024 programme she co-founded is used as the latest written programme. No reversal in 2025-26 was found.

result.bio: François Ruffin, born 18 October 1975 in Calais, is a journalist, documentary maker, essayist and politician. He founded the newspaper Fakir in 1999 and directed the documentary Merci patron! (2016, César for best documentary 2017). He has been deputy for the Somme's 1st constituency since 2017, elected under the LFI label and sitting in the LFI group without being a formal party member; after breaking with Jean-Luc Mélenchon he left LFI on 4 July 2024 and joined the ecologist group (EcoS). He became president of Debout ! on 28 June 2025 and announced on 26 January 2026 that he was standing in the left primary. According to Wikipedia's Debout ! article, the primary was later cancelled and the party then planned to put him forward directly for the presidency.

offices.office: Deputy for Somme, 1st constituency (elected 2017, re-elected 2022 and 2024; LFI group 2017-2024, ecologist group from July 2024)
Secretary of the Economic Affairs Commission, Assemblée nationale

legal.case: Civil defamation suit at the Amiens tribunal over the portrayal of a resident in his 2006 book Quartier Nord. Wikipedia reports that he was found liable (condamné). No primary court source was available.

Ruffin was a victim, not a defendant. LVMH paid Bernard Squarcini's firm Kyrnos to surveil Ruffin and Fakir (March 2015 to February 2016). LVMH settled through a EUR 10 million CJIP, approved on 17 December 2021. On 7 March 2025 the Paris court convicted Squarcini, among other charges, and sentenced him to 4 years (2 of them custodial), a EUR 200,000 fine and a 5-year professional ban. His lawyers said he would appeal.
The HATVP observed that his asset declaration undervalued his audiovisual production company by EUR 431,973. This was an administrative observation, and no criminal proceedings are reported.

delivery.what: Directed the documentary Merci patron! (2016) about LVMH and Bernard Arnault, which won the 2017 César. As a deputy he tabled a high volume of amendments (4,098 in his first term, nearly all rejected). He keeps the net SMIC from his pay and gives about EUR 3,000 a month to associations. He also directed his public party-funding allocation to the PCF.
delivery.assessment: Wikipedia reports a high volume of amendments and commission interventions (162). It also reports low attendance in his first year: he was the least present LFI deputy at votes (22%), and he was among the least present in commission. Few texts of his own were adopted. No roll-call review and no assessment from outlets of different leanings could be obtained.

delivery.what: Called for a united left front in June 2024, which became the Nouveau Front populaire. He then left LFI on 4 July 2024 and joined the ecologist group.
delivery.assessment: Wikipedia describes it as a split with Mélenchon over a deep moral and electoral disagreement. No outlet of a different leaning was consulted.

media_portrayal.left_media: Not verified, because search was unavailable.
media_portrayal.right_media: Not verified, because search was unavailable.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Per Wikipedia, outlets describe him as increasingly independent of LFI and as seeking to reconnect the left with working-class voters. Reported criticisms include low attendance in his first year, Fakir staff doubling as parliamentary collaborators (2017), and a 2018 Le Monde piece by Abel Mestre about ambiguous rhetorical references, which he disputed.

positions.summary: Her campaign's international doctrine (Feb 2026) says Ukraine must be supported 'sans relâche' militarily, with seized Russian assets funding military aid; her party's group voted for the March 2025 Assemblée resolution reinforcing support to Ukraine.

Ukraine has a right to defend itself

positions.summary: The doctrine calls for durable security guarantees for Ukraine including deploying European troops at its borders or on its territory in a deterrent posture.

result.bio: David Lisnard, born 2 February 1969 in Limoges, is a graduate of Sciences Po Bordeaux (class of 1992) and has been mayor of Cannes since 5 April 2014 (re-elected 2020 and March 2026). He was elected president of the Association des maires de France on 17 November 2021 and re-elected on 22 November 2023. He belonged to the RPR, UMP and Les Républicains, became an LR vice-president on 28 June 2025, and left LR on 31 March 2026. He announced on RTL on 21 January 2026 that he would run for president in 2027 under the banner of his movement Nouvelle Énergie (founded 2014, launched nationally in June 2021); an Ifop/Le Figaro poll in June 2026 gave him about 2% in the first round.

offices.office: General/departmental councillor, Alpes-Maritimes (canton Cannes-Est, then Cannes-2 from 2015)
Vice-president of the Alpes-Maritimes general/departmental council (tourism delegation)

President of the Association des maires de France (AMF)

delivery.what: Cannes municipal management: debt reduced by about 55.5 million euros between 2014 and 2019 (Nice-Matin, 30 Dec 2019, as cited by Wikipedia), and an expanded video-surveillance network described as one of France's densest, alongside a reorganised municipal police (Le Point, 2 June 2015, as cited by Wikipedia).
delivery.assessment: These figures are reported by regional and centre-right press as achievements. No critical or left-leaning assessment was found in the sources consulted, so the balance is limited.

delivery.what: July/August 2016 municipal order banning beachwear 'ostentatiously showing a religious affiliation' (the so-called burkini ban), and 2020 Covid-era disinfection of Cannes beaches with hydrogen peroxide (three days, 8,400 euros) plus some streets with bleach at the end of March 2020.
delivery.assessment: On 26 August 2016 the Conseil d'Etat ruled a similar order (Villeneuve-Loubet) illegal, and in May 2018 the city of Cannes was ordered to reimburse a fine issued under its order; this was an administrative/municipal matter, not a case against him personally. The disinfection went ahead despite advice from the Health Ministry and the Haut Conseil de la santé publique.

media_portrayal.neutral_media: Le Monde (9 April 2026, as cited by Wikipedia) presents his candidacy as an autonomous liberal offer on the right, a configuration not seen since Alain Madelin's 2002 candidacy, and notes that his liberalism struggles to convince within the right.

sources.quote: au moins 200 milliards en trajectoire, dont 40 affectés au désendettement

verification_notes: Context: the WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200). Verification relied on fetching primary sources directly: the unenouvelleenergie.fr programme pages, its 62 campaign FAQ pages (updated 3 Oct 2026), and the Bayeux speech PDF of 17 Jun 2026.
Source caveat: the campaign FAQ pages are campaign paraphrases with dated quotes attributed to Lisnard. They are not independent outlets, and cross-lean corroboration could not be done.
monvote2027.fr is an aggregator whose 'quotes' are partly its own inferences, e.g. imm7 and sec3. simulateur-lisnard2027.fr describes itself as 'Site non officiel' and was not cited.

sec1: +2 medium -> +2 high: confirmed on the primary security page.
sec2: +2 medium -> +2 high: confirmed on the primary security page.
sec3: -2 low -> null: there is no evidence on independent oversight; the aggregator read general support for the police as opposition.

sec5: +2 medium -> +1 low: the camera record comes via the aggregator; no AI-surveillance pledge was verified.

eu2: -2 low programme -> -1 low inferred: the 'souveraineté européenne' quote is about sovereignty, not joint borrowing; the programme also backs joint European projects.
eu3: kept null after checking the programme pages.
eu4: kept null after checking the programme pages.
eu5: kept +1 low; evidence type statement -> programme, with the exact primary quote on a referendum in case of supranational blockage.

positions.summary: Lisnard backs strong military support for Ukraine. He has called for a war economy and for helping Ukraine regain a position of strength before any negotiation.

sources.quote: aider l'Ukraine à restaurer une position de force pour négocier
Ce n'est pas par posture morale qu'il nous faut contribuer à un rapport de force favorable à l'Ukraine.

positions.nuance: The most recent explicit statement found is from March 2025. Nothing from 2026 was retrievable because web search was unavailable. He frames aid as a way to strengthen Ukraine's hand before negotiations, while avoiding direct confrontation with Russia. The Feb 2024 quote is as reproduced on his party site and by the MonVote2027 aggregator; the party page fetch did not show the article body.

positions.summary: No statement found on sending French troops to guarantee a ceasefire.
positions.nuance: In the March 2025 Diplomate interview he says France should act 'sans glisser vers une logique d'affrontement direct avec la Russie'. That is not a position on a post-ceasefire reassurance force, so it is not coded.

positions.summary: No statement found on NATO's integrated command.
positions.nuance: The programme speaks of 'une France forte dans ses alliances' but does not mention NATO's integrated command. In the Diplomate interview NATO comes up only in the interviewer's question.

positions.summary: No statement on the EU-Israel association agreement was found. He strongly defends Israel's right to self-defence and called France's recognition of Palestine premature appeasement, which suggests he would oppose suspending the agreement.

sources.outlet: Nouvelle Énergie (Lisnard op-ed, first published by Rupture-mag)
sources.quote: cette reconnaissance prématurée désarme la France diplomatiquement
Son droit à se défendre est légitime

positions.nuance: Inferred from adjacent positions only. He still calls a two-state peace 'l'horizon nécessaire'.

positions.summary: He calls for raising defence spending to 3.5% of GDP.

sources.quote: porter son budget de la défense à 3,5 % du PIB
Pour atteindre 3 % du PIB, il faudrait porter ce budget autour de 100 milliards d'euros par an

positions.nuance: The March 2026 piece criticises the current 2% of GDP as insufficient and works out what 3% would cost. Corroboration from an outlet of a different lean was not possible because search was unavailable.

positions.summary: He wants a universal, short (about three months) military service in barracks and in uniform.

sources.quote: Il doit être universel, court pour des raisons financières – d'une durée de trois mois? -, en caserne et en uniforme.

positions.nuance: 'Universal' implies compulsory. The duration is only floated, with a question mark.

positions.summary: No statement found on lifting sanctions on Russia in exchange for peace.
positions.nuance: In the March 2025 Diplomate interview, sanctions appear only in the interviewer's question.

positions.summary: He signed a mayors' op-ed calling for an end to the national obligation to create low-emission zones (ZFE).

sources.outlet: Le Figaro (collective op-ed, republished by Nouvelle Énergie)
sources.quote: la suppression de l'obligation nationale d'instaurer les zones à faibles émissions

positions.nuance: Coded +1 rather than +2 because the op-ed asks to end the national obligation, which would leave cities free to keep ZFE. It does not ask to ban them outright. It is a collective text that he co-signed.

positions.summary: The programme rejects French over-transposition of EU rules on crop-protection products, calls for regulatory alignment with the single market, and favours 'reasoned' science-based use of pesticides.

sources.quote: en finir avec les surtranspositions françaises, l'alignement réglementaire avec le marché commun
l'usage raisonné des phytosanitaires sur base scientifique

positions.nuance: The programme also demands that products banned in France be banned in imports too ('Ce que nous interdisons ici ne doit plus être autorisé là-bas'). That is a mirror-clause demand. It does not endorse unilateral French bans.

positions.summary: No primary source found on the 2035 end of sales of new combustion cars.
positions.nuance: The MonVote2027 aggregator codes him 'tout à fait contre', citing simulateur-lisnard2027.fr. I could not confirm that the simulator is official, because its About page is template text. Its ecology page did not mention 2035 when fetched. He also denounces 'nouveaux fascistes verts' in the March 2025 manifesto, but that is too general to code.

positions.summary: The programme requires green taxation to be offset by equal tax cuts elsewhere. A 2023 column of his attacks short-haul flight restrictions. Both point to opposition to higher taxes on air travel.

sources.quote: la fiscalité environnementale doit respecter trois règles : d'abord se faire à taxation totale constante
Lignes aériennes : le train-train démago-technocratique (title only)

positions.nuance: No explicit statement on kerosene or private jets was found. The 2023 column's body could not be retrieved; only its critical title was seen. The tax-neutrality rule does not strictly rule out a revenue-neutral air tax, hence -1 with low confidence.

positions.summary: He rejects degrowth and wants climate solutions that respect development, within an 'ecological market economy'.

sources.quote: s'appuyant sur les sciences, l'éducation, le bon sens, le respect du développement, bien plus que sur la décroissance
une « économie écologique de marché » qui ne cède pas « aux nouveaux fascistes verts »

positions.nuance: He does not explicitly rank growth above climate, but he consistently refuses trade-offs that would sacrifice growth. Hence -1 rather than -2.

positions.summary: He calls for 'a first series of six EPRs' plus SMR deployment, and for stopping the dismantling of reactors. This implies more new reactors beyond the first six.

sources.quote: une première série de six EPR
réinvestir les sommes ainsi économisées dans des projets d'avenir, en particulier les nouvelles technologies nucléaires

positions.nuance: No explicit number beyond six large reactors was found, hence +1. The 'first series' wording and the SMR plan point beyond the six EPR2.

positions.summary: He wants nuclear power as the backbone of decarbonised electricity and to stop the planned dismantling of reactors.

sources.quote: arrêter le plan de démantèlement

positions.nuance: His position is consistent. In the March 2025 manifesto he also criticises the closure of Fessenheim.

positions.summary: The programme would end out-of-market support for renewables and redirect the money to nuclear. That is a partial move against new wind farms, though not a halt.

sources.quote: la France a développé ces dernières années une stratégie d'« énergies renouvelables » dérogatoires aux prix du marché

positions.nuance: Coded as partial support because ending subsidies is weaker than suspending wind development. No statement specific to wind turbines was found.

positions.summary: No statement found on leaving the European electricity market.
positions.nuance: Not found in the programme pages or FAQ pages checked.

positions.summary: The programme reforms the Fifth Republic's practice: it refocuses the president against 'hyperprésidentialisme' and strengthens Parliament's oversight role. It does not call for a new constitution or a Sixth Republic.

sources.quote: le rôle du Président de la République doit être recentré sur son statut constitutionnel

positions.nuance: Reform within the current constitution is taken as mild opposition to a new parliamentary constitution. He also proposes a constitutional referendum to reorganise the territory into provinces, which is a territorial change, not a regime change.

positions.summary: No statement found on proportional representation.
positions.nuance: The MonVote2027 aggregator lists 'plutôt contre' but cites no source. Not coded.

positions.summary: No statement found on a citizens' initiative referendum (RIC).
positions.nuance: The aggregator notes only that the programme does not mention the RIC. Silence is not coded.

positions.summary: No statement found on Article 49.3.
positions.nuance: Not found in the programme or FAQ pages.

positions.summary: He proposes widening the scope of Article 11 of the Constitution so that voters can decide on immigration by referendum.

sources.quote: élargissement [...] du champ de l'article onze de la Constitution

positions.nuance: This covers immigration only. No mention of justice was found. He announced '4 référendums' in May 2025, but their content sits in images that could not be read. The quote is fragmentary as rendered.

positions.summary: He opposes a right to active assistance in dying, calling it a 'major anthropological shift', and proposes 4,000 more palliative-care beds instead.

sources.quote: David Lisnard dénonce un « basculement anthropologique majeur » qu'impliquerait une loi sur l'euthanasie active.

positions.nuance: No 2026 restatement was found because search was unavailable. The source text is the outlet's description of his video statement.

positions.summary: No statement found on banning the headscarf in all public spaces.
positions.nuance: His Dec 2025 op-ed limits the absence of religious signs to places 'où la République instruit, juge ou administre', and his programme targets universities. As mayor he banned the burkini on Cannes beaches in 2016, but the Conseil d'État invalidated similar bans. None of this amounts to a general public-space ban, and nothing coded here.

positions.summary: The programme calls for banning the veil at university. Nothing was found on mothers accompanying school trips.

sources.quote: interdiction du voile à l'université

sources.outlet: Rupture-mag op-ed by Lisnard (republished by Nouvelle Énergie)
sources.quote: L'absence de tout signe religieux ostensible doit prévaloir partout où la République instruit, juge ou administre.

positions.nuance: He supports the university half of the statement only, hence +1. School-trip parents are not mentioned.

positions.summary: He wants new restrictions, notably a veil ban at universities. He attacks a 'multiculturalist' reading of laïcité and treats the university veil, burkinis and pool time slots as political Islamist advances.

sources.outlet: Rupture-mag op-ed by Lisnard (republished by Nouvelle Énergie)
sources.quote: Chaque voile à l'université – qui n'a pas vocation à être un lieu de manifestation identitaire mais un sanctuaire de la raison
interdiction du voile à l'université

positions.nuance: The statement rejects any further restriction of citizens' religious expression. He explicitly proposes one, so he is coded -2.

positions.summary: No statement found on surrogacy (GPA).
positions.nuance: The MonVote2027 aggregator lists 'tout à fait contre' with no source. Not coded.

positions.summary: No statement found on school uniforms.
positions.nuance: Not in the education programme or the school FAQ.

positions.summary: His model is a single body of contract teachers recruited by school heads, within deep public-spending cuts. Mass hiring to cut class sizes is not part of it.

sources.quote: Un corps unique d'enseignants contractuels, recrutés sur concours national, sera progressivement mis en place

positions.nuance: Inferred. He does not explicitly reject mass hiring.

positions.summary: The programme creates excellence classes in maths and science in every académie, a form of grouping pupils by level.

sources.quote: Des classes d'excellence en mathématiques et en sciences seront créées dans chaque académie

positions.nuance: These are selective excellence classes at académie level, not ability groups within every collège. Partial support, hence +1.

positions.summary: He proposes a universal education voucher with equal public funding for public and private schools, and abolishing school catchment areas. This is the opposite of cutting private-school funding.

sources.quote: un financement public équivalent, que la famille choisisse l'enseignement public ou privé
Donnons à tous les parents les bonnes informations sur les établissements

positions.nuance: The position is consistent across the programme and the FAQ.

positions.summary: No retrievable statement on abolishing Parcoursup or university selection.
positions.nuance: He wrote an L'Opinion column titled 'Parcoursup du combattant', but its body was not retrievable from the republished page, so it is not coded.

positions.summary: He opposes regulating where doctors can set up practice. He prefers differentiated reimbursement and training more doctors.

sources.quote: Je suis contre la régulation [...] plus on mettra des contraintes sur les médecins, plus ils se barrent à l'étranger
Nous proposons un conventionnement différencié

positions.nuance: The programme uses incentives: better reimbursement in under-served areas.

positions.summary: No statement found on medical franchises or patient co-payments.
positions.nuance: Not in the health programme, the FAQ or the simulator page.

positions.summary: He wants to free the housing market and would challenge the ALUR law, the legal basis for rent control.

sources.quote: Je remettrais en cause les lois 'SRU', 'Alur', 'Climat' et 'Résilience'
Il faut absolument libérer le marché, lui permettre de redevenir la base de la production de logements

positions.nuance: He does not name rent control explicitly. Opposition is clear from his call to free the market and to challenge the law that created rent control.

positions.summary: His liberal programme favours mixed public-private solutions and deregulation, which suggests support for more competition. No statement on transport or energy was found.

sources.quote: des recrutements contractuels souples, y compris passerelles public-privé

positions.nuance: Inferred from his general doctrine. Nothing was found on rail or energy competition specifically.
